647	    RTensor tC_rSFD;
648	    GTensor tC_gSFD;
649	    STensor sAmaxs;
650	    CoordGTensor tC_cSFD;
651	    ThrResidue residue_tC_cSFD;
652	    Params const* params_ptr;
653	    ElementCompute norm_constant;
654	    ElementCompute norm_constant_scaled_down;
655	    TileCoordMN tile_coord_mn;
656	    int thread_idx;
657	    static constexpr int NumCollaboratingThreads = decltype(size(TiledCopy_{}))::value;
658	    static_assert(NumCollaboratingThreads % NumThreadsPerWarpGroup == 0);
659	    static constexpr int NumCollaboratingWarpGroups = NumCollaboratingThreads / NumThreadsPerWarpGroup;
660	    static_assert(NumCollaboratingWarpGroups == 2,
661	                  "SM120 epilogue currently only supports two warp groups collaborating.");
662	    static_assert(SFVecSize == 16 || SFVecSize == 32 || SFVecSize == 64, "SF vector size must be either 16, 32 or 64.");
663	
664	    template <class ElementAccumulator, class ElementInput>
665	    CUTLASS_DEVICE auto
666	    visit(Array<ElementAccumulator, FragmentSize> const& frg_acc,
667	          int epi_v,
668	          int epi_m,
669	          int epi_n,
670	          Array<ElementInput, FragmentSize> const& frg_input) {
671	      return frg_input;
672	    }
673	
674	    template <class SmemTensor, class SyncFn, class VTensor>
675	    CUTLASS_DEVICE void
676	    reduce(SmemTensor&& smem_buffer, SyncFn const& sync_fn, int epi_m, int epi_n, bool is_last_iteration, VTensor visit_results) {
677	      /*
678	      Accumulator fragments are distributed across threads/quads in different warps. For column major, the
679	      reduction happens along M dimension. For SFVector = 32, we have:
680	
681	              8 elements               8 elements             8 elements               8 elements
682	      +  <----------------------><----------------------><----------------------><---------------------->
683	      |     Warp 0 Quad 0           Warp 4 Quad 0           Warp 0 Quad 0           Warp 4 Quad 0
684	      |     Warp 0 Quad 1           Warp 4 Quad 1           Warp 0 Quad 1           Warp 4 Quad 1
685	      |     ...                     ...                     ...                     ...
686	    1 |     Warp 0 Quad 7           Warp 4 Quad 7           Warp 0 Quad 7           Warp 4 Quad 7
687	    6 |     Warp 0 Quad 0           Warp 4 Quad 0           Warp 0 Quad 0           Warp 4 Quad 0
688	      |     Warp 0 Quad 1           Warp 4 Quad 1           Warp 0 Quad 1           Warp 4 Quad 1
689	      |     ...                     ...                     ...                     ...
690	      +     Warp 0 Quad 7           Warp 4 Quad 7           Warp 0 Quad 7           Warp 4 Quad 7
691	      |     Warp 1 Quad 0           Warp 5 Quad 0           Warp 1 Quad 0           Warp 5 Quad 0
692	      |     Warp 1 Quad 1           Warp 5 Quad 1           Warp 1 Quad 1           Warp 5 Quad 1
693	    1 |     ...                     ...                     ...                     ...
694	    6 |     Warp 1 Quad 7           Warp 5 Quad 7           Warp 1 Quad 7           Warp 5 Quad 7
695	      |     Warp 1 Quad 0           Warp 5 Quad 0           Warp 1 Quad 0           Warp 5 Quad 0
696	      |     Warp 1 Quad 1           Warp 5 Quad 1           Warp 1 Quad 1           Warp 5 Quad 1
697	      |     ...                     ...                     ...                     ...
698	      |     Warp 1 Quad 7           Warp 5 Quad 7           Warp 1 Quad 7           Warp 5 Quad 7
699	
700	                    <same pattern for warps 2/3 and 6/7 for the next set of 32 rows>
701	
702	      In this case, colum-wise scale factors are cooperatively reduced across 8 threads from 2 warps.
703	      Each column first computes its own, local absolute maximum and then shares this with the
704	      corresponding threads in the other warp. In this case, a reduction through shared memory is needed.
705	
706	      For SFVector = 64, the reduction happens inside 4 warps: warp 0/1/2/3 and warp 4/5/6/7.
707	      */
708	
709	      // Accumulator fragments consist of two elements from two different columns of a 16x8 MMA output
710	      static constexpr int RowsPerThreadAccFrag = 2;
711	      static constexpr int ColsPerThreadAccFrag = 2;
712	      static_assert(FragmentSize == (ColsPerThreadAccFrag * RowsPerThreadAccFrag));
713	
714	      static constexpr int NumThreadsPerCol = NumThreadsPerWarp / NumThreadsPerQuad;
715	      constexpr int WarpsPerSF = SFVecSize / NumThreadsPerCol / ColsPerThreadAccFrag;
716	      static_assert(WarpsPerSF == 1 || WarpsPerSF == 2 || WarpsPerSF == 4, "Only one, two or four warps are allowed in reduction.");
717	
718	      auto warp_idx = thread_idx / NumThreadsPerWarp;
719	      auto thread_idx_in_warp = thread_idx % NumThreadsPerWarp;
720	
721	      cutlass::maximum_absolute_value_reduction<ElementCompute, true> amax_op;
722	      cutlass::multiplies<ElementCompute> mul;
723	
724	      auto synchronize = [&] () {
725	        // When WarpsPerSF equals 1, data processing is inside warp, there is no needs to have the sync.
726	        static constexpr bool NoSyncNeeded = (WarpsPerSF == 1);
727	        if(NoSyncNeeded)
728	          return;
729	        cutlass::arch::NamedBarrier::sync(NumCollaboratingThreads, cutlass::arch::ReservedNamedBarriers::EpilogueBarrier);
730	      };
731	
732	      CUTLASS_PRAGMA_UNROLL
733	      for(int mma_in_epi = 0; mma_in_epi < size<1>(tC_rSFD)*size<2>(tC_rSFD); ++mma_in_epi) {
734	
735	        CUTLASS_PRAGMA_UNROLL
736	        for (int sf_id = 0; sf_id < ColsPerThreadAccFrag; ++sf_id) {
737	
738	          //
739	          // Compute amax for this scale factor
740	          //
741	          ElementCompute amax{0};
742	
743	          // Compute amax among vals owned by this thread for this vector
744	          auto acc_frg = visit_results(mma_in_epi);
745	          amax = amax_op(amax, acc_frg[sf_id]);
746	          amax = amax_op(amax, acc_frg[sf_id + ColsPerThreadAccFrag]);
747	
748	          // At this point, each thread has computed the amax of the values that it owns for this SF vector.
749	          // We now need to compute the amax across threads. Because SM120 narrow-precision MMAs have 16x8 output
750	          // size with a quad owning two rows, we know that 8 threads in one column will own all of the 16 elements
751	          // to be reduced via amax. Therefore, we can use warp shuffle intrinsics among threads to compute the amax.
752	          CUTLASS_PRAGMA_UNROLL
753	          for (int i = 1; i < NumThreadsPerCol; ++i) {
754	            auto amax_other = __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, amax, (i * NumThreadsPerQuad));
755	            amax = amax_op(amax, amax_other);
756	          }
757	
758	          // At this point, all threads in the quad have the amax for the elements of the accumulator owned by its
759	          // threads that should be used in computing the amax for this SF.
760	          if (thread_idx_in_warp < NumThreadsPerQuad && WarpsPerSF != 1) {
761	            sAmaxs(thread_idx_in_warp, warp_idx) = amax;
762	          }
763	
764	          synchronize();
765	
766	          // Get the amax broadcasted by the warp with which we share.
767	          // For cooperative kernels, when scale factor vector size is 32 (WarpsPerSF equals 2),
768	          // warp 0 shares with 1, warp2 shares with 2, etc.
769	          // When vector size is 64 (WarpsPerSF equals 4), warp 0 shares with 1/2/3, and 4 shares with 5/6/7.
770	          // When vector size is 16, no needs to swap between warps.
771	          if constexpr (2 == WarpsPerSF) {
772	            auto amax_other = sAmaxs(thread_idx % NumThreadsPerQuad, warp_idx ^ 1);
773	            amax = amax_op(amax, amax_other);
774	          }
775	          else if constexpr (4 == WarpsPerSF) {
776	            auto amax_other1 = sAmaxs(thread_idx % NumThreadsPerQuad, warp_idx ^ 1);
777	            auto amax_other2 = sAmaxs(thread_idx % NumThreadsPerQuad, warp_idx ^ 2);
778	            auto amax_other3 = sAmaxs(thread_idx % NumThreadsPerQuad, warp_idx ^ 3);
779	            amax = amax_op(amax, amax_other1);
780	            amax_other2 = amax_op(amax_other2, amax_other3);
781	            amax = amax_op(amax, amax_other2);
782	          }
783	          synchronize();
784	
785	          ElementCompute pvscale = mul(amax, norm_constant_scaled_down);
786	          UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor qpvscale = NumericConverter<UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor, ElementCompute>{}(pvscale);
787	          filter(tC_rSFD)(sf_id + mma_in_epi*ColsPerThreadAccFrag) = qpvscale;
788	
789	          //
790	          // Apply the scale factor to the output
791	          //
792	          ElementCompute qpvscale_rcp = [&]() {
793	            if constexpr (cute::is_same_v<UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor, float_ue8m0_t>) {
794	              // UE8M0: Use integer subtraction to do the fast rcp in ue8m0 and then convert to float.
795	              auto e8m0_qpvscale_rcp = cutlass::reciprocal_approximate<UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor>{}(qpvscale);
796	              return cutlass::NumericConverter<ElementCompute, UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor>{}(e8m0_qpvscale_rcp);
797	            }
798	            else {
799	              // UE4M3: Do the rcp in fp32 data type.
800	              auto qpvscale_up = cutlass::NumericConverter<ElementCompute, UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor>{}(qpvscale);
801	              return cutlass::reciprocal_approximate_ftz<decltype(qpvscale_up)>{}(qpvscale_up);
802	            }
803	          }();
804	
805	          ElementCompute acc_scale = mul(norm_constant, qpvscale_rcp);
806	          acc_scale = cutlass::minimum_with_nan_propagation<ElementCompute>{}(acc_scale, cutlass::platform::numeric_limits<ElementCompute>::max());
807	
808	          // Compute quantized output values
809	          visit_results(mma_in_epi)[sf_id                       ] = mul(acc_frg[sf_id                       ], acc_scale);
810	          visit_results(mma_in_epi)[sf_id + ColsPerThreadAccFrag] = mul(acc_frg[sf_id + ColsPerThreadAccFrag], acc_scale);
811	        } // end for sf_id
812	      } // end for mma_in_epi
813	
814	      // Since scale factors are computed cooperatively across two or four warps, we only need one thread from the
815	      // cooperating column threads group to write out the data.
816	      bool write_sf = (thread_idx_in_warp < NumThreadsPerQuad);
817	      if constexpr (2 == WarpsPerSF) {
818	        // Output warp {0, 2, 4, 6}.
819	        write_sf &= ((warp_idx & 0x1) == 0);
820	      }
821	      else if constexpr (4 == WarpsPerSF) {
822	        // Output warp {0, 4}.
823	        write_sf &= ((warp_idx & 0x3) == 0);
824	      }
825	      else if constexpr (1 == WarpsPerSF) {
826	        // Output warp {0, 1, ..., 7}. Keep write_sf as is.
827	      }
828	
829	      if (write_sf && elem_less(tC_cSFD(_0{}, _0{}, _0{}, epi_m, epi_n), residue_tC_cSFD)) {
830	        copy_aligned(tC_rSFD, tC_gSFD(_, _, _, _0{}, _0{}, get<0>(tile_coord_mn) + epi_m, get<1>(tile_coord_mn) + epi_n));
831	      }
832	    }
833	  };
834	
835	  template <
836	    bool ReferenceSrc, // do register tensors reference the src or dst layout of the tiled copy
837	    class... Args
838	  >
839	  CUTLASS_DEVICE auto
840	  get_consumer_store_callbacks(ConsumerStoreArgs<Args...> const& args) {
841	
842	    auto [M, N, K, L] = args.problem_shape_mnkl;
843	    auto [m, n, k, l] = args.tile_coord_mnkl;
844	    using Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig= cutlass::detail::Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig<SFVecSize, UMMA::Major::MN>;
845	    UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor* ptr_scale_factor = nullptr;
846	    // If Ptr-Array/Grouped GEMM with BlockScaleFactor per batch/group
847	    if constexpr (!cute::is_same_v<UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor, ElementBlockScaleFactor>) {
848	      ptr_scale_factor = params_ptr->ptr_scale_factor[l];
849	      l = 0;
850	    }
851	    else {
852	      ptr_scale_factor = params_ptr->ptr_scale_factor;
853	    }
854	
855	    static_assert(size<0>(EpilogueTile{}) && ((size<0>(EpilogueTile{}) & (size<1>(EpilogueTile{}) - 1)) == 0),
856	      "Epilogue Tile N should be pow of 2");
857	
858	    auto epi_tile_mn = shape<1>(zipped_divide(make_layout(take<0,2>(args.tile_shape_mnk)), args.epi_tile));
859	    Tensor mSFD = make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(ptr_scale_factor),
860	                    Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig::tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(args.problem_shape_mnkl));
861	
862	    Tensor gSFD = local_tile(mSFD, args.epi_tile, make_coord(_, _,l));               // (EPI_M,EPI_N, #EPI_Ms, #EPI_Ns)
863	    Tensor tCgSFD = sm90_partition_for_epilogue<ReferenceSrc>(        // (CPY,CPY_M,CPY_N,EPI_M,EPI_N,#EPI_Ms, #EPI_Ns)
864	                      gSFD, args.epi_tile, args.tiled_copy, args.thread_idx);
865	    Tensor tCrSFD = make_tensor_like<UnderlyingElementBlockScaleFactor>(take<0,3>(cute::layout(tCgSFD)));    // (CPY,CPY_M,CPY_N)
866	
867	    auto tile_coord_mn = make_coord(m * size<0>(epi_tile_mn), n * size<1>(epi_tile_mn));
868	
869	    // Fetch and compute these during initialization
870	    Tensor mNormConst= make_tensor(make_gmem_ptr(params_ptr->norm_constant_ptr), make_layout(make_shape(M, N, L), params_ptr->norm_constant_stride));
871	    ElementCompute norm_constant = mNormConst(_0{},_0{},l);
872	    ElementCompute fp_max = ElementCompute(cutlass::platform::numeric_limits<ElementOutput>::max());
873	    ElementCompute scale_down_factor = cutlass::reciprocal_approximate_ftz<ElementCompute>{}(fp_max);
874	    ElementCompute norm_constant_scaled_down = cutlass::multiplies<ElementCompute>{}(norm_constant, scale_down_factor);
875	
876	    Tensor sAmaxs = make_tensor(
877	      make_smem_ptr(smem_aux),
878	      make_layout(make_shape(Int<NumThreadsPerQuad>{}, Int<NumSyncWarps>{}))
879	    );
880	
881	    return ConsumerStoreCallbacks(
882	      cute::move(tCrSFD),
883	      cute::move(tCgSFD),
884	      cute::move(sAmaxs),
885	      args.tCcD,
886	      args.residue_tCcD,
887	      params_ptr,
888	      tile_coord_mn,
889	      norm_constant,
890	      norm_constant_scaled_down,
891	      args.thread_idx,
892	      args.tiled_copy);
893	
894	  }
895	};

78	// with exactly one template parameter, and then use that subclass as
79	// the template argument.

89	// With BlockScaleFactor Generation.
90	// 1. Find max of 32 F32 elements
91	// 2. Convert the max to UE8 (or UE4M3) and store the result.
92	// 3. Convert the UE8 (or UE4M3) back to F32 scale.
93	// 4. Reciprocal of F32 scale with MUFU.
94	// 5. Multiply each F32 element with the above reciprocal, then convert to ElementD
95	template<

110	  >;

131	    CtaTileShapeMNK,
132	    EpilogueTile
133	> : Sm120LinearCombRowBlockScaleFactor<SFVecSize, EpilogueTile, CtaTileShapeMNK, FragmentSize, typename cutlass::detail::get_unpacked_element_type<ElementOutput>::type,ElementCompute, ElementBlockScaleFactor, ElementSource, ElementScalar, RoundStyle> {
134	
135	  using Impl = Sm120LinearCombRowBlockScaleFactor<SFVecSize, EpilogueTile, CtaTileShapeMNK, FragmentSize, typename cutlass::detail::get_unpacked_element_type<ElementOutput>::type,ElementCompute, ElementBlockScaleFactor, ElementSource, ElementScalar, RoundStyle>;
136

140	        CtaTileShapeMNK,
141	        EpilogueTile
142	  >;
143	  using Operation = typename Sm100Fusion::Operation;
144	
145	  struct Arguments {
146	    ElementScalar alpha = ElementScalar(1);
147	    ElementScalar beta = ElementScalar(0);
148	    ElementScalar const* alpha_ptr = nullptr;
149	    ElementScalar const* beta_ptr = nullptr;
150	    ElementBlockScaleFactor * block_scale_factor_ptr = nullptr;
151	    // A matrix wide constant value to scale the output matrix
152	    // Avoids generating small FP4 values.
153	    using StrideNormConst = Stride<_0,_0,int64_t>;
154	    ElementCompute const* norm_constant_ptr = nullptr;
155	    StrideNormConst dNormConst = {_0{}, _0{}, 0};
156	
157	    using StrideAlpha = Stride<_0,_0,int64_t>;
158	    using StrideBeta  = Stride<_0,_0,int64_t>;
159	    StrideAlpha dAlpha = {_0{}, _0{}, 0};
160	    StrideBeta  dBeta  = {_0{}, _0{}, 0};
161	
162	    operator typename Impl::Arguments() const {
163	      return
164	        {
165	          {
166	            // ternary op : beta * C + (alpha * acc)
167	            {{beta}, {beta_ptr}, {dBeta}}, // leaf args : beta
168	            {},                   // leaf args : C
169	            {                     // binary op : alpha * acc
170	              {{alpha}, {alpha_ptr}, {dAlpha}}, // leaf args : alpha
171	              {},                 // leaf args : acc
172	              {}                  // binary args : multiplies
173	            },                    // end binary op
174	            {}                    // ternary args : multiply_add
175	          },
176	          {block_scale_factor_ptr, norm_constant_ptr, dNormConst} // BlockScaleFactor args
177	        };   // end ternary op
178	    }
179	  };
180	  
181	  // Ctor inheritance
182	  using Impl::Impl;
183	};

266	  is_producer_load_needed() const {
267	    auto const& scale_op = get<0>(Impl::ops);
268	    auto const& added_op = get<2>(Impl::ops);
269	    if constexpr (detail::IsScalarBroadcast<InputScaleOp>::value && not is_void_v<ElementSource>) {
270	      return (get<2>(scale_op.params_ptr->dScalar[0]) != 0 && scale_op.params_ptr->scalar_ptrs[0] != nullptr) ||
271	              is_C_load_needed() ||

283	    auto const& added_op = get<2>(Impl::ops);
284	    return (not scale_op.is_zero() && src_op.is_C_load_needed()) || added_op.is_C_load_needed();

62	template <
63	  bool ReferenceSrc, // do register tensors reference the src or dst layout of the tiled copy
64	  class CtaTileMN,
65	  class EpilogueTile,
66	  class TiledCopy
67	>
68	CUTLASS_HOST_DEVICE
69	constexpr auto
70	sm90_partition_for_epilogue(
71	    CtaTileMN cT,          // (CTA_M,CTA_N,...)
72	    EpilogueTile epi_tile, // (EPI_TILE_M,EPI_TILE_N)
73	    TiledCopy tiled_copy,
74	    int thread_idx) {
75	  ThrCopy thread_copy = tiled_copy.get_thread_slice(thread_idx);
76	  Tensor cT_epi = flat_divide(cT, epi_tile);                                 // (EPI_TILE_M,EPI_TILE_N,EPI_M,EPI_N,...)
77	  if constexpr (ReferenceSrc) {
78	    return thread_copy.partition_S(cT_epi);                                        // (CPY,CPY_M,CPY_N,EPI_M,EPI_N,...)
79	  }
80	  else {
81	    return thread_copy.partition_D(cT_epi);                                        // (CPY,CPY_M,CPY_N,EPI_M,EPI_N,...)
82	  }
83	}
84	
85	template <
86	  bool ReferenceSrc, // do register tensors reference the src or dst layout of the tiled copy
87	  class Engine, class LayoutMNL,
88	  class TileShapeMNK,
89	  class TileCoordMNKL,
90	  class EpilogueTile,
91	  class TiledCopy
92	>
93	CUTLASS_HOST_DEVICE
94	constexpr auto
95	sm90_partition_for_epilogue(
96	    Tensor<Engine, LayoutMNL> mT,  // (M,N,L)
97	    TileShapeMNK tile_shape_mnk,   // (CTA_M,CTA_N,CTA_K)
98	    TileCoordMNKL tile_coord_mnkl, // (m,n,k,l)
99	    EpilogueTile epi_tile,         // (EPI_TILE_M,EPI_TILE_N)
100	    TiledCopy tiled_copy,
101	    int thread_idx) {
102	  auto [m, n, k, l] = tile_coord_mnkl;
103	  auto coord_shape =
104	      make_coord(m, n, l)
105	    ;
106	  Tensor cT = local_tile(mT, take<0,2>(tile_shape_mnk), coord_shape);                                  // (CTA_M,CTA_N)
107	  Tensor tCcT =
108	    sm90_partition_for_epilogue<ReferenceSrc>(cT, epi_tile, tiled_copy, thread_idx);   // (CPY,CPY_M,CPY_N,EPI_M,EPI_N)
109	
110	  return tCcT;
111	}

119	//
120	// Producer load callbacks, called by the epilogue load warp.
121	// Operations usually only define this if TMA load is needed. Most operations will reuse this empy implementation
122	// Load callbacks are responsible for issuing corresponding mbarrier expect-tx ops for any TMA loads issued, but
123	// are not responsible for issuing the producer_commit barrier arrival, which is issued by the collective instead
124	// If this is non-empty, is_producer_load_needed must be true.
125	//
126	template <class CallbacksTuple>
127	struct ProducerLoadCallbacksImpl {
128	  // Callbacks can store non-persistent variables (e.g. tensors) or copies of persistent variables
129	  CallbacksTuple callbacks_tuple;
130	
131	  // Before entry of the subtile load loop
132	  CUTLASS_DEVICE void
133	  begin() {
134	    for_each(callbacks_tuple,
135	      [&] (auto& callbacks) CUTLASS_LAMBDA_FUNC_INLINE {
136	        callbacks.begin();
137	      }
138	    );
139	  }
140	
141	  // Entry of the subtile load loop. Aux loads usually performed here
142	  // Upon entry the producer acquire of the current subtile lock has completed.
143	  // Upon exit all TMA loads for this subtile must have been issued, with corresponding expect-tx operations
144	  CUTLASS_DEVICE void
145	  step(uint64_t* full_mbarrier_ptr, int epi_m, int epi_n, int load_iteration, bool issue_tma_load) {
146	    for_each(callbacks_tuple,
147	      [&] (auto& callbacks) CUTLASS_LAMBDA_FUNC_INLINE {
148	        callbacks.step(full_mbarrier_ptr, epi_m, epi_n, load_iteration, issue_tma_load);
149	      }
150	    );

52	"""
53	High-performance persistent blockscaled contiguous grouped dense GEMM with gather and SwiGLU fusion
54	(C = up * silu(gate), where up and gate come from interleaved weight matrix B)
55	example for the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture using CUTE DSL.
56	
57	This kernel performs FC1 layer computation with SwiGLU activation fusion:
58	1. GEMM: acc = alpha * (SFA * A[token_ids]) * (SFB * B)
59	2. SwiGLU: C = up * silu(gate), where up/gate are extracted from interleaved acc (granularity=64)
60	3. Optional Quant: When c_dtype is Float4E2M1FN, generates scale factor C and quantizes output
61	
62	- Matrix A is MxKx1, A can be row-major("K"), ValidM is composed of valid m in different groups
63	- Matrix B is NxKxL, B can be column-major("K"), L is grouped dimension (number of experts)
64	  - B weights are interleaved: [up_0:64, gate_64:128, up_128:192, gate_192:256, ...]
65	- Matrix C is Mx(N/2)x1, C can be row-major("N"), N is halved due to SwiGLU fusion
66	- Matrix SFA layout is filled internally according to A shape and BlockScaledBasicChunk,
67	  which has M×ceil_div(K, sf_vec_size)×1 elements
68	- Matrix SFB layout is filled internally according to B shape and BlockScaledBasicChunk,
69	  which has N×ceil_div(K, sf_vec_size)×L elements
70	- Token ID mapping tensor enables gather operation for A and SFA
71	
72	Matrix A/C Memory Layout Diagrams:
73	
74	   ```
75	    Group 0    Group 1   Group 2
76	   -+---------+---------+---------+
77	    |         |         |         |
78	   K| ValidM0 | ValidM1 | ValidM2 |
79	    |         |         |         |
80	   -+---------+---------+---------+
81	    |<-        ValidM           ->|
82	   ```
83	   Note: the Group(L) dimension will be flatted into M dimension, and the rest Group(L) size is 1.
84	         each ValidM will be aligned to 256 or 128. The alignment is determined by the mma_tiler_mn parameter.
85	         For NVFP4, 2CTA, the alignment is 256. For NVFP4, 1CTA, the alignment is 128.
86	
87	This GEMM kernel supports the following features:
88	    - Utilizes LDGSTS (Load Global to Shared with Swizzle) for A and SFA with gather operation
89	    - Utilizes Tensor Memory Access (TMA) for B and SFB matrices
90	    - Utilizes Blackwell's tcgen05.mma for matrix multiply-accumulate (MMA) operations
91	    - Implements TMA multicast with cluster to reduce L2 memory traffic
92	    - Support persistent tile scheduling to better overlap memory load/store with mma between tiles
93	    - Support warp specialization to avoid explicit pipelining between mainloop load and mma
94	
95	This GEMM works as follows:
96	1. SCHEDULER warp (warp 10): Dispatches tile information to all consumer warps via tile_info_pipeline.
97	2. LDGSTS A/SFA warps (warps 4-7):
98	    - Load A matrix from global memory (GMEM) to shared memory (SMEM) using LDGSTS instructions with gather.
99	    - Load SFA (scale factor A) from GMEM to SMEM using LDGSTS instructions.
100	    - Uses token_id_mapping to perform permutation/gather during load.
101	3. TMA B/SFB warp (warp 9):
102	    - Load B and SFB matrices from GMEM to SMEM using TMA operations with multicast.
103	4. MMA warp (warp 8):
104	    - Load scale factor A/B from shared memory (SMEM) to tensor memory (TMEM) using tcgen05.cp instruction.
105	    - Perform matrix multiply-accumulate (MMA) operations using tcgen05.mma instruction.
106	5. EPILOGUE warps (warps 0-3):
107	    - Load two accumulator subtiles (up and gate) from tensor memory (TMEM) to registers (RMEM) using tcgen05.ld.
108	    - Apply alpha scaling: up_scaled = alpha * up, gate_scaled = alpha * gate
109	    - Compute SwiGLU activation: output = up_scaled * silu(gate_scaled), where silu(x) = x * sigmoid(x)
110	    - If c_dtype is Float4E2M1FN: generate scale factor C (SFC) and quantize output
111	    - Type convert output to c_dtype.
112	    - Store C matrix from registers (RMEM) to shared memory (SMEM) to global memory (GMEM) with TMA operations.
113	
114	SM100 tcgen05.mma.kind.block_scale instructions operate as follows:
115	- Read matrix A from SMEM
116	- Read matrix B from SMEM
117	- Read scalefactor A from TMEM
118	- Read scalefactor B from TMEM
119	- Write accumulator to TMEM
120	The accumulator in TMEM must then be loaded to registers before writing back to GMEM.
121	
122	Constraints:
123	* Supported input data types: mxf8, mxf4, nvf4
124	  see detailed valid dtype combinations in below Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel class documentation
125	* A/B tensor must have the same data type, mixed data type is not supported (e.g., mxf8 x mxf4)
126	* Mma tiler M must be 128 or 256(use_2cta_instrs)
127	* Mma tiler N must be 64/128/192/256
128	* Cluster shape M/N must be positive and power of 2, total cluster size <= 16
129	* Cluster shape M must be multiple of 2 if Mma tiler M is 256(use_2cta_instrs)
130	* The contiguous dimension of A/B/C tensors must be at least 16 bytes aligned,
131	  i.e, number of elements is a multiple of 16 and 32 for Float8 and Float4, respectively.
132	
133	CUDA Graph Support:
134	* For CUDA graph support, the tile_idx_to_expert_idx, token_id_mapping, A/C matrices,
135	  and scale factor A can be padded to a larger size
136	  (e.g., permuted_m = m*topK + num_local_experts*(256-1),
137	  example: 4096*8 + (256/32)*255 = 34808)
138	* Use create_tensors() with permuted_m parameter to automatically pad:
139	  - tile_idx_to_expert_idx: padded for invalid tiles (set to -2e9 for padding tiles)
140	  - token_id_mapping: padded to permuted_m size (invalid tokens set to -1)
141	  - A matrix: padded to permuted_m rows (padding rows contain dummy data)
142	  - C matrix: padded to permuted_m rows (output buffer for cuda_graph)
143	  - Scale factor A: padded to match A matrix dimensions
144	* Kernel handling of padding:
145	  - Scheduler warp checks if tile_idx >= num_non_exiting_tiles to exit
146	  - Only valid tiles (tile_idx < num_non_exiting_tiles) are written to tile_info pipeline
147	  - LDGSTS warps use token_id_mapping predicates to skip invalid tokens (token_id == -1)
148	  - When no more valid tiles exist, outer loop exits and calls producer_tail()
149	  - Consumer warps process only valid tiles from pipeline
150	  - No deadlock or synchronization issues

116	template <typename Gemm>
117	void run_gemm(
118	    torch::Tensor out,
119	    torch::Tensor out_scale,
120	    torch::Tensor A,
121	    torch::Tensor B,
122	    torch::Tensor A_scale,
123	    torch::Tensor B_scale,
124	    torch::Tensor global_scale,
125	    int m,
126	    int n,
127	    int k) {
128	  Gemm gemm;
129	  auto args = prepare_args<Gemm>(
130	      out.data_ptr(), out_scale.data_ptr(), A.data_ptr(), B.data_ptr(),
131	      A_scale.data_ptr(), B_scale.data_ptr(),
132	      static_cast<float const*>(global_scale.data_ptr()), m, n, k);
133	
134	  auto can = gemm.can_implement(args);
135	  TORCH_CHECK(can == cutlass::Status::kSuccess,
136	              "can_implement failed: ", cutlass::cutlassGetStatusString(can));
137	
138	  size_t workspace_size = gemm.get_workspace_size(args);
139	  auto workspace = torch::empty(
140	      {static_cast<long>(workspace_size)},
141	      torch::TensorOptions().device(A.device()).dtype(torch::kUInt8));
142	
143	  cudaStream_t stream = at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream().stream();
144	  auto init = gemm.initialize(args, workspace.data_ptr(), stream);
145	  TORCH_CHECK(init == cutlass::Status::kSuccess,
146	              "initialize failed: ", cutlass::cutlassGetStatusString(init));
147	  auto status = gemm.run(args, workspace.data_ptr(), stream, nullptr, true);
148	  TORCH_CHECK(status == cutlass::Status::kSuccess,
149	              "run failed: ", cutlass::cutlassGetStatusString(status));
150	}
151	
152	}  // namespace
153	
154	std::vector<torch::Tensor> fp4_gemm_blockscale_out(
155	    torch::Tensor A,
156	    torch::Tensor B,
157	    torch::Tensor A_scale,
158	    torch::Tensor B_scale,
159	    torch::Tensor global_scale,
160	    int64_t n) {
161	  TORCH_CHECK(A.is_cuda() && B.is_cuda() && A_scale.is_cuda() && B_scale.is_cuda());
162	  TORCH_CHECK(A.scalar_type() == torch::kUInt8);
163	  TORCH_CHECK(B.scalar_type() == torch::kUInt8);
164	  TORCH_CHECK(A.dim() == 2 && B.dim() == 2);
165	  int64_t m = A.size(0);
166	  int64_t k_packed = A.size(1);
167	  int64_t k = k_packed * 2;
168	  TORCH_CHECK(B.size(0) == n && B.size(1) == k_packed);
169	  TORCH_CHECK(n % 16 == 0);
170	
171	  auto out = torch::empty({m, n / 2}, A.options());
172	  using OutputConfig = cutlass::detail::Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig<16>;
173	  auto sfd_layout = OutputConfig::tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(cute::make_shape(
174	      static_cast<int>(m), static_cast<int>(n), static_cast<int>(k), 1));
175	  int64_t sfd_bytes = cute::cosize(sfd_layout);
176	  auto out_scale = torch::empty(
177	      {sfd_bytes},
178	      torch::TensorOptions().device(A.device()).dtype(torch::kUInt8));
179	
180	  using Gemm = typename Fp4BlockscaleEpilogueGemm<128, 128, 128>::Gemm;
181	  run_gemm<Gemm>(out, out_scale, A, B, A_scale, B_scale, global_scale, m, n, k);
182	  return {out, out_scale};
183	}
184	
185	int64_t required_sfd_bytes(int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k) {
186	  using OutputConfig = cutlass::detail::Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig<16>;
187	  auto sfd_layout = OutputConfig::tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(cute::make_shape(
188	      static_cast<int>(m), static_cast<int>(n), static_cast<int>(k), 1));
189	  return cute::cosize(sfd_layout);
190	}
191	
192	PYBIND11_MODULE(TORCH_EXTENSION_NAME, m) {
193	  m.def("fp4_gemm_blockscale_out", &fp4_gemm_blockscale_out);
194	  m.def("required_sfd_bytes", &required_sfd_bytes);
195	}

34	    """当前 GPU 是否支持 FP4 Marlin fallback (CUDA SM >= 75)。"""

52	def _nvfp4_compute_scale_factor(marlin_scales: torch.Tensor) -> float:
53	    """计算 power-of-2 rescale factor，使得所有非零 weight_scale * 2^7 >= 2。
54	
55	    防 dequant_fp8_scales<nv_bfloat162> BF16 widening underflow（vLLM PR #34577）：
56	    当 weight_scale * 2^7 < 2 时，S0E5M3 表示 MSB=0，BF16 widening 会被错误展开为 ~2^-112
57	    导致下游 dequant 退化。返回 sf >= 1.0 (Python float, power of 2)。
58	    """
59	    ws_float = marlin_scales.float() * (2**7)
60	    nonzero_mask = ws_float > 0
61	    if nonzero_mask.any():
62	        min_val = ws_float[nonzero_mask].min()
63	        if min_val < 2:
64	            sf = (2 / min_val).log2().ceil().exp2()
65	            assert (ws_float[nonzero_mask] * sf <= 448 * (2**7)).all(), (
66	                "NVFP4 scale dynamic range 太大，rescale 会溢出 E4M3 上限"
67	            )
68	            return sf.item()
69	    return 1.0

63	  auto runKernel = [&](void* workspace) {
64	    gemmRunner.gemm(out.data_ptr(), mat1.data_ptr(), mat2.data_ptr(), mat1Scale.data_ptr(),
65	                    mat2Scale.data_ptr(), static_cast<float*>(globalScale.data_ptr()), m, n, k,
66	                    batch_count, gemmConfig, reinterpret_cast<char*>(workspace),
67	                    required_workspace_size, get_stream(mat1.device()));
68	  };
69	
70	  if (provided_workspace_size < required_workspace_size) {
71	    Tensor new_workspace =
72	        alloc_tensor({required_workspace_size}, DLDataType{kDLInt, 8, 1}, mat1.device());
73	    runKernel(new_workspace.data_ptr());
74	  } else {
75	    runKernel(workspace_buffer.data_ptr());
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	constexpr auto FLOAT4_E2M1X2 = dl_uint8;  // uint8_t
80	constexpr auto SF_DTYPE = dl_uint8;       // uint8_t
81	
82	void fp4_bmm_impl(TensorView mat1, TensorView mat2, TensorView mat1Scale, TensorView mat2Scale,
83	                  TensorView globalScale, TensorView out, TensorView workspace_buffer,
84	                  int64_t tactic) {
85	  // Validate inputs
86	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat1.dtype(), FLOAT4_E2M1X2) << "mat1 must be FLOAT4_E2M1X2 (uint8)";
87	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat2.dtype(), FLOAT4_E2M1X2) << "mat2 must be FLOAT4_E2M1X2 (uint8)";
88	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat1Scale.dtype(), SF_DTYPE) << "mat1Scale must be SF_DTYPE (uint8)";
89	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat2Scale.dtype(), SF_DTYPE) << "mat2Scale must be SF_DTYPE (uint8)";
90	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(globalScale.dtype(), dl_float32) << "globalScale must be float";
91	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat1.device().device_type, kDLCUDA) << "mat1 must be on CUDA device";
92	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat2.device().device_type, kDLCUDA) << "mat2 must be on CUDA device";
93	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat1Scale.device().device_type, kDLCUDA) << "mat1Scale must be on CUDA device";
94	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat2Scale.device().device_type, kDLCUDA) << "mat2Scale must be on CUDA device";
95	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(globalScale.device().device_type, kDLCUDA)
96	      << "globalScale must be on CUDA device";
97	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(out.device().device_type, kDLCUDA) << "out must be on CUDA device";
98	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(workspace_buffer.device().device_type, kDLCUDA)
99	      << "workspace_buffer must be on CUDA device";
100	
101	  // Check device consistency
102	  CHECK_DEVICE(mat1, mat2);
103	  CHECK_DEVICE(mat1, mat1Scale);
104	  CHECK_DEVICE(mat1, mat2Scale);
105	  CHECK_DEVICE(mat1, globalScale);
106	  CHECK_DEVICE(mat1, out);
107	  CHECK_DEVICE(mat1, workspace_buffer);
108	
109	  // Get dimensions
110	  int64_t b = 1;
111	  int64_t m, k_packed, n;
112	
113	  if (mat1.ndim() == 2) {
114	    m = mat1.size(0);
115	    k_packed = mat1.size(1);
116	  } else if (mat1.ndim() == 3) {
117	    b = mat1.size(0);
118	    m = mat1.size(1);
119	    k_packed = mat1.size(2);
120	  } else {
121	    TVM_FFI_ICHECK(false) << "mat1 must be 2D or 3D tensor";
122	  }
123	
124	  if (mat2.ndim() == 2) {
125	    n = mat2.size(0);
126	    TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat2.size(1), k_packed) << "mat2.size(1) must match mat1.size(-1)";
127	  } else if (mat2.ndim() == 3) {
128	    TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat2.size(0), b) << "Batch dimensions must match";
129	    n = mat2.size(1);
130	    TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(mat2.size(2), k_packed) << "mat2.size(2) must match mat1.size(-1)";
131	  } else {
132	    TVM_FFI_ICHECK(false) << "mat2 must be 2D or 3D tensor";
133	  }
134	
135	  // k_packed stores 2 FP4 values per byte
136	  int64_t k = k_packed * 2;
137	
138	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(globalScale.numel(), 1) << "globalScale must be a scalar tensor";
139	
140	  // Configure the kernel
141	  CutlassGemmConfig config =
142	      (tactic >= 0) ? getFp4GemmConfig(m, n, k, tactic)
143	                    : CutlassGemmConfig(CutlassTileConfigSM120::CtaShape128x128x128B,
144	                                        MainloopScheduleType::AUTO, EpilogueScheduleType::AUTO,
145	                                        ClusterShape::ClusterShape_1x1x1);
146	
147	  // Validate output dimensions
148	  std::vector<int64_t> out_shape =
149	      (b > 1) ? std::vector<int64_t>{b, m, n} : std::vector<int64_t>{m, n};
150	  TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(out.ndim(), out_shape.size())
151	      << "out must have " << out_shape.size() << " dimensions";
152	  for (size_t i = 0; i < out_shape.size(); ++i) {
153	    TVM_FFI_ICHECK_EQ(out.size(i), out_shape[i])
154	        << "out.size(" << i << "): expected " << out_shape[i] << ", got " << out.size(i);
155	  }
156	
157	  switch (encode_dlpack_dtype(out.dtype())) {
158	    case float16_code:
159	      runGemm<half>(out, mat1, mat2, mat1Scale, mat2Scale, globalScale, m, n, k, b, config,
160	                    workspace_buffer);
161	      break;
162	    case bfloat16_code:
163	      runGemm<__nv_bfloat16>(out, mat1, mat2, mat1Scale, mat2Scale, globalScale, m, n, k, b, config,
164	                             workspace_buffer);
165	      break;
166	    default:
167	      TVM_FFI_ICHECK(false) << "out_dtype must be one of fp16/bf16.";
168	  }
169	}
170	
171	}  // namespace
172	
173	void fp4_gemm(TensorView mat1, TensorView mat2, TensorView mat1Scale, TensorView mat2Scale,
174	              TensorView globalScale, TensorView out, TensorView workspace_buffer, int64_t tactic) {
175	  fp4_bmm_impl(mat1, mat2, mat1Scale, mat2Scale, globalScale, out, workspace_buffer, tactic);
176	}
177	
178	int64_t fp4_gemm_tactic_num() {
179	  static const int64_t totalTactics =
180	      CutlassFp4GemmRunner<__nv_bfloat16, FP4GemmType::W4A4_NVFP4_NVFP4>{}.getConfigs().size();
181	  return totalTactics;
182	}
183	
184	}  // namespace torch_ext

159	def get_reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm_row_indices(x) -> torch.Tensor:
160	    """
161	    Reorders rows in the gemm/MOE_gemm weight matrix for min-latency
162	    [r0, r1, r2, r3, ..., rN/2, r(N/2+1), .. r(N-1)]
163	    to
164	    [r0, rN/2, r1, rN/2+1, ..., r(N/2-1), r(N-1)]
165	    """
166	    assert x.dim() == 2, f"x should be a 2D tensor, not {x.dim()}"
167	    M, K = x.shape
168	    assert M % 2 == 0, f"x.shape[0] must be even, not {M}"
169	
170	    row_indices = torch.arange(M, dtype=torch.long)
171	
172	    # We split into top half and bottom half, but if M is odd,
173	    # the bottom half is one row larger.
174	    top = row_indices[: (M + 1) // 2]  # round up
175	    bot = row_indices[(M + 1) // 2 :]  # remainder
176	
177	    # Create the output
178	    permuted_row_indices = torch.empty_like(row_indices)
179	
180	    # We'll place rows of `top` and `bot` in alternation
181	    permuted_row_indices[0::2] = top
182	    permuted_row_indices[1::2] = bot
183	
184	    return permuted_row_indices
185	
186	
187	def reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm(x):
188	    """
189	    PyTorch implementation of trt-llm gen `reorderRowsForGatedActGemm`
190	    """
191	    row_indices = get_reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm_row_indices(x)
192	
193	    permute = lambda x: x[row_indices]
194	
195	    return permute(x)
196

199	    M, K = input_tensor.shape
200	    assert K % blockK == 0, "K must be divisible by blockK"

52	"""
53	High-performance persistent blockscaled contiguous grouped dense GEMM with gather and SwiGLU fusion
54	(C = up * silu(gate), where up and gate come from interleaved weight matrix B)
55	example for the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture using CUTE DSL.
56	
57	This kernel performs FC1 layer computation with SwiGLU activation fusion:
58	1. GEMM: acc = alpha * (SFA * A[token_ids]) * (SFB * B)
59	2. SwiGLU: C = up * silu(gate), where up/gate are extracted from interleaved acc (granularity=64)
60	3. Optional Quant: When c_dtype is Float4E2M1FN, generates scale factor C and quantizes output
61	
62	- Matrix A is MxKx1, A can be row-major("K"), ValidM is composed of valid m in different groups
63	- Matrix B is NxKxL, B can be column-major("K"), L is grouped dimension (number of experts)
64	  - B weights are interleaved: [up_0:64, gate_64:128, up_128:192, gate_192:256, ...]
65	- Matrix C is Mx(N/2)x1, C can be row-major("N"), N is halved due to SwiGLU fusion
66	- Matrix SFA layout is filled internally according to A shape and BlockScaledBasicChunk,
67	  which has M×ceil_div(K, sf_vec_size)×1 elements
68	- Matrix SFB layout is filled internally according to B shape and BlockScaledBasicChunk,
69	  which has N×ceil_div(K, sf_vec_size)×L elements
70	- Token ID mapping tensor enables gather operation for A and SFA
71	
72	Matrix A/C Memory Layout Diagrams:
73	
74	   ```
75	    Group 0    Group 1   Group 2
76	   -+---------+---------+---------+
77	    |         |         |         |
78	   K| ValidM0 | ValidM1 | ValidM2 |
79	    |         |         |         |
80	   -+---------+---------+---------+
81	    |<-        ValidM           ->|
82	   ```
83	   Note: the Group(L) dimension will be flatted into M dimension, and the rest Group(L) size is 1.
84	         each ValidM will be aligned to 256 or 128. The alignment is determined by the mma_tiler_mn parameter.
85	         For NVFP4, 2CTA, the alignment is 256. For NVFP4, 1CTA, the alignment is 128.
86	
87	This GEMM kernel supports the following features:
88	    - Utilizes LDGSTS (Load Global to Shared with Swizzle) for A and SFA with gather operation
89	    - Utilizes Tensor Memory Access (TMA) for B and SFB matrices
90	    - Utilizes Blackwell's tcgen05.mma for matrix multiply-accumulate (MMA) operations
91	    - Implements TMA multicast with cluster to reduce L2 memory traffic
92	    - Support persistent tile scheduling to better overlap memory load/store with mma between tiles
93	    - Support warp specialization to avoid explicit pipelining between mainloop load and mma
94	
95	This GEMM works as follows:
96	1. SCHEDULER warp (warp 10): Dispatches tile information to all consumer warps via tile_info_pipeline.
97	2. LDGSTS A/SFA warps (warps 4-7):
98	    - Load A matrix from global memory (GMEM) to shared memory (SMEM) using LDGSTS instructions with gather.
99	    - Load SFA (scale factor A) from GMEM to SMEM using LDGSTS instructions.
100	    - Uses token_id_mapping to perform permutation/gather during load.
101	3. TMA B/SFB warp (warp 9):
102	    - Load B and SFB matrices from GMEM to SMEM using TMA operations with multicast.
103	4. MMA warp (warp 8):
104	    - Load scale factor A/B from shared memory (SMEM) to tensor memory (TMEM) using tcgen05.cp instruction.
105	    - Perform matrix multiply-accumulate (MMA) operations using tcgen05.mma instruction.
106	5. EPILOGUE warps (warps 0-3):
107	    - Load two accumulator subtiles (up and gate) from tensor memory (TMEM) to registers (RMEM) using tcgen05.ld.
108	    - Apply alpha scaling: up_scaled = alpha * up, gate_scaled = alpha * gate
109	    - Compute SwiGLU activation: output = up_scaled * silu(gate_scaled), where silu(x) = x * sigmoid(x)
110	    - If c_dtype is Float4E2M1FN: generate scale factor C (SFC) and quantize output
111	    - Type convert output to c_dtype.
112	    - Store C matrix from registers (RMEM) to shared memory (SMEM) to global memory (GMEM) with TMA operations.
113	
114	SM100 tcgen05.mma.kind.block_scale instructions operate as follows:
115	- Read matrix A from SMEM
116	- Read matrix B from SMEM
117	- Read scalefactor A from TMEM
118	- Read scalefactor B from TMEM
119	- Write accumulator to TMEM
120	The accumulator in TMEM must then be loaded to registers before writing back to GMEM.
121	
122	Constraints:
123	* Supported input data types: mxf8, mxf4, nvf4
124	  see detailed valid dtype combinations in below Sm100BlockScaledPersistentDenseGemmKernel class documentation
125	* A/B tensor must have the same data type, mixed data type is not supported (e.g., mxf8 x mxf4)
126	* Mma tiler M must be 128 or 256(use_2cta_instrs)
127	* Mma tiler N must be 64/128/192/256
128	* Cluster shape M/N must be positive and power of 2, total cluster size <= 16
129	* Cluster shape M must be multiple of 2 if Mma tiler M is 256(use_2cta_instrs)
130	* The contiguous dimension of A/B/C tensors must be at least 16 bytes aligned,
131	  i.e, number of elements is a multiple of 16 and 32 for Float8 and Float4, respectively.
132	
133	CUDA Graph Support:
134	* For CUDA graph support, the tile_idx_to_expert_idx, token_id_mapping, A/C matrices,
135	  and scale factor A can be padded to a larger size
136	  (e.g., permuted_m = m*topK + num_local_experts*(256-1),
137	  example: 4096*8 + (256/32)*255 = 34808)
138	* Use create_tensors() with permuted_m parameter to automatically pad:
139	  - tile_idx_to_expert_idx: padded for invalid tiles (set to -2e9 for padding tiles)
140	  - token_id_mapping: padded to permuted_m size (invalid tokens set to -1)
141	  - A matrix: padded to permuted_m rows (padding rows contain dummy data)
142	  - C matrix: padded to permuted_m rows (output buffer for cuda_graph)
143	  - Scale factor A: padded to match A matrix dimensions
144	* Kernel handling of padding:
145	  - Scheduler warp checks if tile_idx >= num_non_exiting_tiles to exit
146	  - Only valid tiles (tile_idx < num_non_exiting_tiles) are written to tile_info pipeline
147	  - LDGSTS warps use token_id_mapping predicates to skip invalid tokens (token_id == -1)
148	  - When no more valid tiles exist, outer loop exits and calls producer_tail()
149	  - Consumer warps process only valid tiles from pipeline
150	  - No deadlock or synchronization issues
151	* Consumer warps check initial tile against num_non_exiting_tiles and set
152	  is_valid_tile=False if tile_idx >= num_non_exiting_tiles
153	* Only rows within (aligned_groupm[0]+aligned_groupm[1]+...) contain valid data
154	* Padding rows in C matrix will not be written by the kernel
155	"""
156

159	def hooked_PersistentTileSchedulerParams_init(
160	    self,
161	    problem_shape_ntile_mnl: cute.Shape,
162	    cluster_shape_mnk: cute.Shape,
163	    swizzle_size: int = 1,
164	    raster_along_m: bool = True,
165	    *,
166	    loc=None,
167	    ip=None,
168	):
169	    if cluster_shape_mnk[2] != 1:
170	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported cluster_shape_k {cluster_shape_mnk[2]}")
171	    if swizzle_size < 1:
172	        raise ValueError(f"expect swizzle_size >= 1, but get {swizzle_size}")
173	
174	    self.problem_shape_ntile_mnl = problem_shape_ntile_mnl
175	    # cluster_shape_mnk is kept for reconstruction
176	    self._cluster_shape_mnk = cluster_shape_mnk
177	    self.cluster_shape_mn = cluster_shape_mnk[:2]
178	    self.swizzle_size = swizzle_size

182	    # Apply swizzle if swizzle_size > 1
183	    if swizzle_size > 1:
184	        problem_shape_ncluster_mnl = cute.round_up(
185	            self.problem_layout_ncluster_mnl.shape,
186	            (1, swizzle_size, 1) if raster_along_m else (swizzle_size, 1, 1),
187	        )
188	
189	        if raster_along_m:
190	            self.problem_layout_ncluster_mnl = cute.make_layout(
191	                (
192	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0],
193	                    (swizzle_size, problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1] // swizzle_size),
194	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[2],
195	                ),
196	                stride=(
197	                    swizzle_size,
198	                    (1, swizzle_size * problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0]),
199	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0] * problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1],
200	                ),
201	                loc=loc,
202	                ip=ip,
203	            )
204	        else:
205	            self.problem_layout_ncluster_mnl = cute.make_layout(
206	                (
207	                    (swizzle_size, problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0] // swizzle_size),
208	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1],
209	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[2],
210	                ),
211	                stride=(
212	                    (1, swizzle_size * problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1]),
213	                    swizzle_size,
214	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0] * problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1],
215	                ),
216	                loc=loc,

222	    if swizzle_size == 1:

225	        )

228	                problem_shape_ncluster_mnl,

231	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0],
232	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0] * problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1],
233	                ),
234	                loc=loc,
235	                ip=ip,
236	            )
237	        else:
238	            self.problem_layout_ncluster_mnl = cute.make_layout(
239	                problem_shape_ncluster_mnl,
240	                stride=(
241	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1],
242	                    1,
243	                    problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[0] * problem_shape_ncluster_mnl[1],
244	                ),
245	                loc=loc,
246	                ip=ip,
247	            )

250	        )
251	        cluster_count_m = self.problem_layout_ncluster_mnl.shape[0]
252	        cluster_count_n = self.problem_layout_ncluster_mnl.shape[1]
253

275	def hooked_get_cluster_work_idx_with_fastdivmod(
276	    self, current_work_linear_idx: Int32, *, loc=None, ip=None
277	) -> Tuple[Int32, Int32, Int32]:
278	    work_iteration, work_unit_id = divmod(
279	        current_work_linear_idx, self.params.batch_fdd
280	    )
281	
282	    if self.params._raster_along_m:
283	        # raster_along_m=True means column major (m is fastest)
284	        # First, get cluster_m using cluster_shape_m_fdd
285	        cluster_n_batch, cluster_m = divmod(
286	            work_unit_id, self.params.cluster_shape_m_fdd
287	        )
288	
289	        # Then decode cluster_n_batch to get cluster_n and batch_l using FastDivmod
290	        batch_l, cluster_n = divmod(cluster_n_batch, self.params.cluster_shape_n_fdd)
291	    else:
292	        # raster_along_m=False means row major (n is fastest)
293	        # First, get cluster_n using cluster_shape_n_fdd
294	        cluster_m_batch, cluster_n = divmod(
295	            work_unit_id, self.params.cluster_shape_n_fdd

314	class BlockScaledContiguousGatherGroupedGemmKernel:
315	    """This class implements contiguous grouped matrix multiplication with gather operation and SwiGLU fusion
316	    for FC1 layer computation (C = up * silu(gate), where up/gate come from interleaved GEMM result).
317	
318	    The computation flow:
319	    1. GEMM: acc = alpha * (SFA * A[token_ids]) * (SFB * B)
320	    2. SwiGLU: C = up * silu(gate), extracted from interleaved acc with granularity=64
321	    3. Optional Quant: When c_dtype is Float4E2M1FN, generates SFC and quantizes output
322	
323	    Note: Output C has N/2 columns since pairs of (up, gate) are combined by SwiGLU.
324	
325	    Key Features:
326	    - Uses LDGSTS instructions for loading A and SFA matrices with gather/permutation capability
327	    - Uses TMA (Tensor Memory Access) for loading B and SFB matrices with multicast
328	    - Token ID mapping enables efficient gather operation during A/SFA load
329	    - SwiGLU activation fusion in epilogue (up * silu(gate) with interleaved weights)
330	    - Optional quantization fusion for Float4E2M1FN output with scale factor generation
331	    - Warp specialization: Scheduler (warp 10), A Sync Transform (warp 11, only used when
332	      use_2cta_instrs is True), LDGSTS A/SFA (warps 4-7), TMA B/SFB (warp 9), MMA (warp 8),
333	      Epilogue (warps 0-3)
334	
335	    :param sf_vec_size: Scalefactor vector size (16 for NVF4, 32 for MXF4/MXF8).
336	    :type sf_vec_size: int
337	    :param mma_tiler_mn: Shape of the Matrix Multiply-Accumulate (MMA) tile (M,N).
338	        Note: use_2cta_instrs is automatically inferred from mma_tiler_mn[0]
339	        (True when M=256, False when M=128).
340	    :type mma_tiler_mn: Tuple[int, int]
341	    :param cluster_shape_mn: Cluster dimensions (M,N) for parallel processing
342	    :type cluster_shape_mn: Tuple[int, int]
343	    :param vectorized_f32: Whether to use vectorized f32x2 operations for better performance.
344	    :type vectorized_f32: bool
345	
346	    :note: In current version, A and B tensor must have the same data type
347	        - i.e., Float8E4M3FN for A and Float8E5M2 for B is not supported
348	
349	    :note: Supported combinations of A/B data types, SF data typs and SF vector size:
350	        - MXF8: A/B: Float8E5M2/Float8E4M3FN + SF: Float8E8M0FNU + sf_vec_size: 32
351	        - MXF4: A/B: Float4E2M1FN + SF: Float8E8M0FNU + sf_vec_size: 32
352	        - NVF4: A/B: Float4E2M1FN + SF: Float8E8M0FNU/Float8E4M3FN + sf_vec_size: 16
353	
354	    :note: Supported accumulator data types:
355	        - Float32
356	
357	    :note: Supported C data types:
358	        - Float32
359	        - Float16/BFloat16
360	        - Float8E4M3FN/Float8E5M2
361	        # Note: Float4E2M1FN output includes SFC generation and quantization support for internal testing.
362	        - Float4E2M1FN (with scale factor generation)
363	
364	    :note: Constraints:
365	        - MMA tiler M must be 128 or 256 (use_2cta_instrs)
366	        - MMA tiler N must be 64/128/192/256
367	        - Cluster shape M must be multiple of 2 if Mma tiler M is 256
368	        - Cluster shape M/N must be positive and power of 2, total cluster size <= 16
369	        - Also, Cluster shape M/N must be <= 4 for scale factor multicasts due to limited size of scale factors
370	
371	    Example:
372	        >>> # Note: use_2cta_instrs is auto-inferred from mma_tiler_mn[0]
373	        >>> # (True when M=256, False when M=128)
374	        >>> gemm = BlockScaledContiguousGatherGroupedGemmKernel(
375	        ...     sf_vec_size=16,
376	        ...     mma_tiler_mn=(256, 128),  # use_2cta_instrs=True since M=256
377	        ...     cluster_shape_mn=(2, 1),
378	        ...     vectorized_f32=True,
379	        ... )
380	        >>> gemm(
381	        ...     a=a_tensor,
382	        ...     b=b_tensor,
383	        ...     c=c_tensor,
384	        ...     sfa=sfa_tensor,
385	        ...     sfb=sfb_tensor,
386	        ...     sfc_tensor=None,

388	        ...     tile_idx_to_expert_idx=tile_idx_to_expert_idx,

392	        ...     alpha=alpha,
393	        ...     max_active_clusters=max_active_clusters,
394	        ...     stream=stream,
395	        ... )
396	    """
397	
398	    def __init__(
399	        self,
400	        sf_vec_size: int,

159	def get_reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm_row_indices(x) -> torch.Tensor:
160	    """
161	    Reorders rows in the gemm/MOE_gemm weight matrix for min-latency
162	    [r0, r1, r2, r3, ..., rN/2, r(N/2+1), .. r(N-1)]
163	    to
164	    [r0, rN/2, r1, rN/2+1, ..., r(N/2-1), r(N-1)]
165	    """
166	    assert x.dim() == 2, f"x should be a 2D tensor, not {x.dim()}"
167	    M, K = x.shape
168	    assert M % 2 == 0, f"x.shape[0] must be even, not {M}"
169	
170	    row_indices = torch.arange(M, dtype=torch.long)
171	
172	    # We split into top half and bottom half, but if M is odd,
173	    # the bottom half is one row larger.
174	    top = row_indices[: (M + 1) // 2]  # round up
175	    bot = row_indices[(M + 1) // 2 :]  # remainder
176	
177	    # Create the output
178	    permuted_row_indices = torch.empty_like(row_indices)
179	
180	    # We'll place rows of `top` and `bot` in alternation
181	    permuted_row_indices[0::2] = top
182	    permuted_row_indices[1::2] = bot
183	
184	    return permuted_row_indices
185	
186	
187	def reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm(x):
188	    """
189	    PyTorch implementation of trt-llm gen `reorderRowsForGatedActGemm`
190	    """
191	    row_indices = get_reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm_row_indices(x)
192	
193	    permute = lambda x: x[row_indices]
194	
195	    return permute(x)
196

198	def convert_to_block_layout(input_tensor: torch.Tensor, blockK: int) -> torch.Tensor:
199	    M, K = input_tensor.shape
200	    assert K % blockK == 0, "K must be divisible by blockK"
201	    return input_tensor.view(M, K // blockK, blockK).permute(1, 0, 2).contiguous()

257	        )
258	
259	        # cluster_shape_m_fdd: Used to decode work_unit_id to cluster coordinates
260	        self.cluster_shape_m_fdd = cute.fast_divmod_create_divisor(
261	            cluster_count_m, loc=loc, ip=ip
262	        )
263	
264	        # cluster_shape_n_fdd: Used for the second level decomposition
265	        self.cluster_shape_n_fdd = cute.fast_divmod_create_divisor(
266	            cluster_count_n, loc=loc, ip=ip
267	        )
268	    else:
269	        # FastDivmod not applicable with swizzling, set to None
270	        self.batch_fdd = None
271	        self.cluster_shape_m_fdd = None
272	        self.cluster_shape_n_fdd = None

275	def hooked_get_cluster_work_idx_with_fastdivmod(
276	    self, current_work_linear_idx: Int32, *, loc=None, ip=None
277	) -> Tuple[Int32, Int32, Int32]:
278	    work_iteration, work_unit_id = divmod(
279	        current_work_linear_idx, self.params.batch_fdd
280	    )
281	
282	    if self.params._raster_along_m:
283	        # raster_along_m=True means column major (m is fastest)
284	        # First, get cluster_m using cluster_shape_m_fdd
285	        cluster_n_batch, cluster_m = divmod(
286	            work_unit_id, self.params.cluster_shape_m_fdd
287	        )
288	
289	        # Then decode cluster_n_batch to get cluster_n and batch_l using FastDivmod
290	        batch_l, cluster_n = divmod(cluster_n_batch, self.params.cluster_shape_n_fdd)
291	    else:
292	        # raster_along_m=False means row major (n is fastest)
293	        # First, get cluster_n using cluster_shape_n_fdd
294	        cluster_m_batch, cluster_n = divmod(
295	            work_unit_id, self.params.cluster_shape_n_fdd
296	        )
297	
298	        # Then decode cluster_m_batch to get cluster_m and batch_l using FastDivmod
299	        batch_l, cluster_m = divmod(cluster_m_batch, self.params.cluster_shape_m_fdd)
300	
301	    return (cluster_m, cluster_n, batch_l)

314	class BlockScaledContiguousGatherGroupedGemmKernel:
315	    """This class implements contiguous grouped matrix multiplication with gather operation and SwiGLU fusion
316	    for FC1 layer computation (C = up * silu(gate), where up/gate come from interleaved GEMM result).
317	
318	    The computation flow:
319	    1. GEMM: acc = alpha * (SFA * A[token_ids]) * (SFB * B)
320	    2. SwiGLU: C = up * silu(gate), extracted from interleaved acc with granularity=64
321	    3. Optional Quant: When c_dtype is Float4E2M1FN, generates SFC and quantizes output
322	
323	    Note: Output C has N/2 columns since pairs of (up, gate) are combined by SwiGLU.
324	
325	    Key Features:
326	    - Uses LDGSTS instructions for loading A and SFA matrices with gather/permutation capability
327	    - Uses TMA (Tensor Memory Access) for loading B and SFB matrices with multicast
328	    - Token ID mapping enables efficient gather operation during A/SFA load
329	    - SwiGLU activation fusion in epilogue (up * silu(gate) with interleaved weights)
330	    - Optional quantization fusion for Float4E2M1FN output with scale factor generation
331	    - Warp specialization: Scheduler (warp 10), A Sync Transform (warp 11, only used when
332	      use_2cta_instrs is True), LDGSTS A/SFA (warps 4-7), TMA B/SFB (warp 9), MMA (warp 8),
333	      Epilogue (warps 0-3)
334	
335	    :param sf_vec_size: Scalefactor vector size (16 for NVF4, 32 for MXF4/MXF8).
336	    :type sf_vec_size: int
337	    :param mma_tiler_mn: Shape of the Matrix Multiply-Accumulate (MMA) tile (M,N).
338	        Note: use_2cta_instrs is automatically inferred from mma_tiler_mn[0]
339	        (True when M=256, False when M=128).
340	    :type mma_tiler_mn: Tuple[int, int]
341	    :param cluster_shape_mn: Cluster dimensions (M,N) for parallel processing
342	    :type cluster_shape_mn: Tuple[int, int]
343	    :param vectorized_f32: Whether to use vectorized f32x2 operations for better performance.
344	    :type vectorized_f32: bool
345	
346	    :note: In current version, A and B tensor must have the same data type
347	        - i.e., Float8E4M3FN for A and Float8E5M2 for B is not supported
348	
349	    :note: Supported combinations of A/B data types, SF data typs and SF vector size:
350	        - MXF8: A/B: Float8E5M2/Float8E4M3FN + SF: Float8E8M0FNU + sf_vec_size: 32
351	        - MXF4: A/B: Float4E2M1FN + SF: Float8E8M0FNU + sf_vec_size: 32
352	        - NVF4: A/B: Float4E2M1FN + SF: Float8E8M0FNU/Float8E4M3FN + sf_vec_size: 16
353	
354	    :note: Supported accumulator data types:
355	        - Float32
356	
357	    :note: Supported C data types:
358	        - Float32
359	        - Float16/BFloat16
360	        - Float8E4M3FN/Float8E5M2
361	        # Note: Float4E2M1FN output includes SFC generation and quantization support for internal testing.
362	        - Float4E2M1FN (with scale factor generation)
363	
364	    :note: Constraints:
365	        - MMA tiler M must be 128 or 256 (use_2cta_instrs)
366	        - MMA tiler N must be 64/128/192/256
367	        - Cluster shape M must be multiple of 2 if Mma tiler M is 256
368	        - Cluster shape M/N must be positive and power of 2, total cluster size <= 16
369	        - Also, Cluster shape M/N must be <= 4 for scale factor multicasts due to limited size of scale factors
370	
371	    Example:
372	        >>> # Note: use_2cta_instrs is auto-inferred from mma_tiler_mn[0]
373	        >>> # (True when M=256, False when M=128)
374	        >>> gemm = BlockScaledContiguousGatherGroupedGemmKernel(
375	        ...     sf_vec_size=16,
376	        ...     mma_tiler_mn=(256, 128),  # use_2cta_instrs=True since M=256
377	        ...     cluster_shape_mn=(2, 1),
378	        ...     vectorized_f32=True,
379	        ... )
380	        >>> gemm(
381	        ...     a=a_tensor,
382	        ...     b=b_tensor,
383	        ...     c=c_tensor,
384	        ...     sfa=sfa_tensor,
385	        ...     sfb=sfb_tensor,
386	        ...     sfc_tensor=None,
387	        ...     norm_const_tensor=None,
388	        ...     tile_idx_to_expert_idx=tile_idx_to_expert_idx,
389	        ...     tile_idx_to_mn_limit=tile_idx_to_mn_limit,
390	        ...     token_id_mapping_tensor=token_id_mapping_tensor,
391	        ...     num_non_exiting_tiles=num_non_exiting_tiles,
392	        ...     alpha=alpha,
393	        ...     max_active_clusters=max_active_clusters,
394	        ...     stream=stream,
395	        ... )
396	    """
397	
398	    def __init__(
399	        self,
400	        sf_vec_size: int,
401	        mma_tiler_mn: Tuple[int, int],
402	        cluster_shape_mn: Tuple[int, int],
403	        vectorized_f32: bool,
404	        topk: cutlass.Int64,
405	        raster_along_m: bool = False,
406	        enable_pdl: bool = True,
407	    ):
408	        """Initializes the configuration for a Blackwell blockscaled dense GEMM kernel with
409	        gather operation and SwiGLU fusion.
410	
411	        This configuration includes several key aspects:
412	
413	        1.  MMA Instruction Settings (tcgen05):
414	            - acc_dtype: Data types for MMA accumulator.
415	            - mma_tiler_mn: The (M, N) shape of the MMA instruction tiler.
416	            - use_2cta_instrs: Automatically inferred from mma_tiler_mn[0]
417	              (True when M=256, False when M=128).
418	
419	        2.  Cluster Shape:
420	            - cluster_shape_mn: The (ClusterM, ClusterN) shape of the CTA cluster.
421	
422	        3.  Scale Factor Configuration:
423	            - sf_vec_size: Vector size for block-scaled quantization.
424	
425	        4.  Performance Optimization:
426	            - vectorized_f32: Enable vectorized f32x2 operations.
427	
428	        5.  MoE Configuration:
429	            - topk: Number of experts selected per token (used for token ID mapping).
430	
431	        :param sf_vec_size: Vector size for scale factors (16 for NVF4, 32 for MXF4/MXF8).
432	        :type sf_vec_size: int
433	        :param mma_tiler_mn: Tuple (M, N) shape of the MMA instruction.
434	            use_2cta_instrs is automatically set based on M (True if M=256, False if M=128).
435	        :type mma_tiler_mn: Tuple[int, int]
436	        :param cluster_shape_mn: Tuple (ClusterM, ClusterN) shape of the cluster.
437	        :type cluster_shape_mn: Tuple[int, int]
438	        :param vectorized_f32: Enable vectorized f32x2 operations for better performance.
439	        :type vectorized_f32: bool
440	        :param topk: Number of experts selected per token (used for token ID mapping).
441	        :type topk: cutlass.Int64
442	        """
443	
444	        self.sf_vec_size = sf_vec_size
445	        self.enable_pdl = enable_pdl
446	        self.topk = topk
447	        self.acc_dtype = cutlass.Float32
448	        self.use_2cta_instrs = mma_tiler_mn[0] == 256

502	
503	        # Set barrier for cta sync, epilogue sync and tmem ptr sync

116	template <typename Gemm>
117	void run_gemm(
118	    torch::Tensor out,
119	    torch::Tensor out_scale,
120	    torch::Tensor A,
121	    torch::Tensor B,
122	    torch::Tensor A_scale,
123	    torch::Tensor B_scale,
124	    torch::Tensor global_scale,
125	    int m,
126	    int n,
127	    int k) {
128	  Gemm gemm;
129	  auto args = prepare_args<Gemm>(
130	      out.data_ptr(), out_scale.data_ptr(), A.data_ptr(), B.data_ptr(),
131	      A_scale.data_ptr(), B_scale.data_ptr(),
132	      static_cast<float const*>(global_scale.data_ptr()), m, n, k);
133	
134	  auto can = gemm.can_implement(args);
135	  TORCH_CHECK(can == cutlass::Status::kSuccess,
136	              "can_implement failed: ", cutlass::cutlassGetStatusString(can));
137	
138	  size_t workspace_size = gemm.get_workspace_size(args);
139	  auto workspace = torch::empty(
140	      {static_cast<long>(workspace_size)},
141	      torch::TensorOptions().device(A.device()).dtype(torch::kUInt8));
142	
143	  cudaStream_t stream = at::cuda::getCurrentCUDAStream().stream();
144	  auto init = gemm.initialize(args, workspace.data_ptr(), stream);
145	  TORCH_CHECK(init == cutlass::Status::kSuccess,
146	              "initialize failed: ", cutlass::cutlassGetStatusString(init));
147	  auto status = gemm.run(args, workspace.data_ptr(), stream, nullptr, true);
148	  TORCH_CHECK(status == cutlass::Status::kSuccess,
149	              "run failed: ", cutlass::cutlassGetStatusString(status));
150	}

162	  TORCH_CHECK(A.scalar_type() == torch::kUInt8);
163	  TORCH_CHECK(B.scalar_type() == torch::kUInt8);
164	  TORCH_CHECK(A.dim() == 2 && B.dim() == 2);
165	  int64_t m = A.size(0);
166	  int64_t k_packed = A.size(1);
167	  int64_t k = k_packed * 2;
168	  TORCH_CHECK(B.size(0) == n && B.size(1) == k_packed);
169	  TORCH_CHECK(n % 16 == 0);
170	
171	  auto out = torch::empty({m, n / 2}, A.options());
172	  using OutputConfig = cutlass::detail::Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig<16>;
173	  auto sfd_layout = OutputConfig::tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(cute::make_shape(
174	      static_cast<int>(m), static_cast<int>(n), static_cast<int>(k), 1));
175	  int64_t sfd_bytes = cute::cosize(sfd_layout);
176	  auto out_scale = torch::empty(
177	      {sfd_bytes},
178	      torch::TensorOptions().device(A.device()).dtype(torch::kUInt8));
179	
180	  using Gemm = typename Fp4BlockscaleEpilogueGemm<128, 128, 128>::Gemm;
181	  run_gemm<Gemm>(out, out_scale, A, B, A_scale, B_scale, global_scale, m, n, k);
182	  return {out, out_scale};
183	}
184	
185	int64_t required_sfd_bytes(int64_t m, int64_t n, int64_t k) {
186	  using OutputConfig = cutlass::detail::Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig<16>;
187	  auto sfd_layout = OutputConfig::tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(cute::make_shape(
188	      static_cast<int>(m), static_cast<int>(n), static_cast<int>(k), 1));
189	  return cute::cosize(sfd_layout);
190	}

159	def get_reorder_rows_for_gated_act_gemm_row_indices(x) -> torch.Tensor:
160	    """
161	    Reorders rows in the gemm/MOE_gemm weight matrix for min-latency
162	    [r0, r1, r2, r3, ..., rN/2, r(N/2+1), .. r(N-1)]
163	    to
164	    [r0, rN/2, r1, rN/2+1, ..., r(N/2-1), r(N-1)]
165	    """
166	    assert x.dim() == 2, f"x should be a 2D tensor, not {x.dim()}"
167	    M, K = x.shape
168	    assert M % 2 == 0, f"x.shape[0] must be even, not {M}"
169	
170	    row_indices = torch.arange(M, dtype=torch.long)
171	
172	    # We split into top half and bottom half, but if M is odd,
173	    # the bottom half is one row larger.
174	    top = row_indices[: (M + 1) // 2]  # round up
175	    bot = row_indices[(M + 1) // 2 :]  # remainder
176	
177	    # Create the output
178	    permuted_row_indices = torch.empty_like(row_indices)

73	def _split_scale_param(scale):
74	    """Split scale parameter into tensor and scalar components.
75	
76	    Args:
77	        scale: Can be a torch.Tensor (per-head), a scalar float, or None.
78	
79	    Returns:
80	        tuple: (tensor_ptr, scalar_val) where:
81	            - If scale is tensor: (scale, 1.0)
82	            - If scale is scalar: (None, scale)
83	            - If scale is None: (None, 1.0)
84	    """
85	    if scale is None:
86	        return None, 1.0
87	    elif isinstance(scale, torch.Tensor):
88	        return scale, 1.0
89	    else:
90	        return None, float(scale)

36	_MINICPM_PROFILE = os.getenv("SGLANG_MINICPM_PROFILE", "0") == "1"
37	_MINICPM_PROFILE_INTERVAL = max(
38	    1, int(os.getenv("SGLANG_MINICPM_PROFILE_INTERVAL", "64"))
39	)
40	_MINICPM_NVTX = os.getenv("SGLANG_MINICPM_NVTX", "0") == "1"
41	_MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS: dict[str, float] = {}
42	_MINICPM_PROFILE_COUNTS: dict[str, int] = {}
43	
44	
45	def _profile_can_sync() -> bool:
46	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
47	        return False
48	    try:
49	        return not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing()
50	    except RuntimeError:
51	        return False
52	
53	
54	def _profile_begin() -> float:
55	    if _profile_can_sync():
56	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
57	    return time.perf_counter()
58	
59	
60	def _profile_end(start: float, bucket: str):
61	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
62	        return
63	    if _profile_can_sync():
64	        torch.cuda.synchronize()
65	    _MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS[bucket] = _MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS.get(bucket, 0.0) + (
66	        time.perf_counter() - start
67	    ) * 1000.0
68	
69	
70	def _profile_step(counter: str, buckets: tuple[str, ...], label: str):
71	    if not _MINICPM_PROFILE:
72	        return
73	    count = _MINICPM_PROFILE_COUNTS.get(counter, 0) + 1
74	    _MINICPM_PROFILE_COUNTS[counter] = count
75	    if count % _MINICPM_PROFILE_INTERVAL != 0:
76	        return
77	    stats = ", ".join(
78	        f"{bucket}={_MINICPM_PROFILE_TOTALS.get(bucket, 0.0) / count:.3f}ms"
79	        for bucket in buckets
80	    )
81	    print(f"[minicpm-profile] {label} calls={count}, {stats}")

254	        self.head_dim = model_runner.model_config.head_dim
255	        # Query/output data type must stay in compute precision (bf16/fp16);
256	        # only KV cache storage uses the quantized dtype (e.g. fp8_e5m2).

258	        # is not supported in FA2/FA3 backends.

任务：评估剩余 **bitwise** 路线可行性，聚焦两个方向：

1. **跨 8 个 sparse layer 复用 stage1 score**：
   - 当前 8 standard sparse layer = layer id [0, 9, 16, 17, 22, 29, 30, 31]
   - 每层用 **per-layer K1/K2 (compress_k)** 算自己的 score（gP）和 topk
   - 历史 §3.10：相邻 layer ret 完全一致率"首 8K chunk 0.887-0.918，第二个起 0.423-0.476"，不稳定
   - 但完全一致率不等于"近似一致"。如果 ret 80%+ 重叠，且 stage2 sparse FA 对"近邻 topk replace"鲁棒（即少量 page 错替换不影响输出 bitwise），是否可做"score 跨层 lazy 重计算"？看 stage2 是否对 sparse_page_table 内容敏感
   - 找 §3.10 原 commit / probe 代码，看历史是怎么测的；当前 baseline 重测 ret 重叠率是否变了

2. **stage1 launch coalesce / batched chunk**：
   - 当前 64 chunks 顺序处理，每 chunk 8 layers 依次 launch stage1 kernel
   - kernel grid 是 `[bs, n_split, num_q_heads]`？看 `flash_api.cpp:mha_varlen_fwd_stage1` 或 sgl-kernel 源码
   - 能否在一次 kernel launch 内处理 **多个 chunk** 的 stage1？比如 grid 多一维 chunk_id
   - launch overhead vs kernel time 比例：5.571s / 512 calls = **10.9ms / call**（远大于 launch overhead ~5us），coalesce 不太可能有大收益
   - 但是 **CPU side stream sync / wrapper prepare** 可能有节省

3. **Stage1 跨 chunk K2 复用**：
   - K2 = compress_k 输出（stride-64 coarse）
   - 跨 chunk 是 append-only：chunk_i 的 K2 包含 chunk_i-1 全部 + 新 token 的 compress
   - 现状 `compress_k_buffer_prefill_ms=0.03ms/call`（§3.5），已经只算 increment
   - 但 stage1 kernel 内每个 chunk 重新读全部 K2 进行 attention。能否将 K2 reduction 状态保留下来跨 chunk 复用？需重新 derive stage1 算法

503	"""Fused CUDA kernel for sparse_page_table to flashinfer format conversion.
504	
505	This module provides a CUDA graph compatible conversion from MiniCPM's
506	sparse_page_table format to FlashInfer's kv_indices + kv_indptr format.
507	"""
508	
509	import os
510	from typing import Tuple
511	
512	import torch
513	import triton
514	import triton.language as tl
515	
516	
517	# Environment variable to select implementation
518	# Set USE_TRITON_KERNEL=1 to use Triton (CUDA graph compatible)
519	# Set USE_TRITON_KERNEL=0 to use PyTorch reference (slower, not CUDA graph compatible)
520	# Default is "1" - always use Triton kernel for CUDA graph compatibility
521	USE_TRITON_KERNEL = os.environ.get("USE_TRITON_KERNEL", "1") == "1"
522	
523	# Environment variable to enable comparison between PyTorch and Triton implementations
524	# Set COMPARE_PYTORCH_TRITON=1 to validate Triton outputs against PyTorch reference
525	_COMPARISON_ENABLED = os.environ.get("COMPARE_PYTORCH_TRITON", "0") == "1"
526	
527	
528	#
529	# Alternative: Two-kernel approach for better performance with large batches
530	# Kernel 1: Compute cumulative sum (parallel scan)
531	# Kernel 2: Flatten and fill
532	
533	
534	@triton.jit
535	def cumsum_kernel(
536	    cache_seqlens_ptr,
537	    kv_indptr_ptr,
538	    sparse_bs: tl.constexpr,
539	):
540	    """Compute cumulative sum using parallel scan algorithm."""
541	    # Simple sequential implementation for now
542	    # TODO: Implement parallel scan for better performance
543	    cumsum = 0
544	    tl.store(kv_indptr_ptr, 0)
545	
546	    for i in range(sparse_bs):
547	        val = tl.load(cache_seqlens_ptr + i)
548	        cumsum += val
549	        tl.store(kv_indptr_ptr + i + 1, cumsum)
550	
551	
552	@triton.jit
553	def flatten_and_fill_kernel(
554	    sparse_page_table_ptr,
555	    cache_seqlens_ptr,
556	    kv_indptr_ptr,
557	    kv_indices_ptr,
558	    kv_last_page_len_ptr,
559	    max_sparse_tokens: tl.constexpr,
560	    sparse_bs: tl.constexpr,
561	    BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr = 256,
562	):
563	    """Flatten sparse_page_table and fill kv_last_page_len."""
564	    pid = tl.program_id(axis=0)
565	
566	    if pid >= sparse_bs:
567	        return
568	
569	    # Get offset and num_valid
570	    offset = tl.load(kv_indptr_ptr + pid)
571	    num_valid = tl.load(cache_seqlens_ptr + pid)
572	
573	    # Copy valid entries
574	    num_loops = tl.cdiv(num_valid, BLOCK_SIZE)
575	    for i in range(num_loops):
576	        idx = i * BLOCK_SIZE + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE)
577	        mask = idx < num_valid
578	
579	        src_idx = pid * max_sparse_tokens + idx
580	        data = tl.load(sparse_page_table_ptr + src_idx, mask=mask, other=0)
581	
582	        dst_idx = offset + idx
583	        tl.store(kv_indices_ptr + dst_idx, data, mask=mask)
584	
585	    # Fill kv_last_page_len
586	    tl.store(kv_last_page_len_ptr + pid, 1)
587	
588	
589	def convert_sparse_to_flashinfer_two_kernel(
590	    sparse_page_table: torch.Tensor,
591	    cache_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
592	    kv_indptr: torch.Tensor,
593	    kv_indices: torch.Tensor,
594	    kv_last_page_len: torch.Tensor,
595	):
596	    """Two-kernel version for potentially better performance."""
597	    sparse_bs = cache_seqlens.shape[0]
598	    max_sparse_tokens = sparse_page_table.shape[1]
599	
600	    # Kernel 1: Compute cumulative sum
601	    cumsum_kernel[(1,)](
602	        cache_seqlens,
603	        kv_indptr,
604	        sparse_bs=sparse_bs,
605	    )
606	
607	    # Kernel 2: Flatten and fill
608	    BLOCK_SIZE = 256
609	    flatten_and_fill_kernel[(sparse_bs,)](
610	        sparse_page_table,
611	        cache_seqlens,
612	        kv_indptr,
613	        kv_indices,
614	        kv_last_page_len,
615	        max_sparse_tokens=max_sparse_tokens,
616	        sparse_bs=sparse_bs,
617	        BLOCK_SIZE=BLOCK_SIZE,
618	    )
619	
620	    return kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_last_page_len
621	
622	
623	# ============================================================================
624	# PyTorch Reference Implementation (for testing and fallback)
625	# ============================================================================
626	
627	
628	def convert_sparse_to_flashinfer_pytorch(
629	    sparse_page_table: torch.Tensor,
630	    cache_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
631	    kv_indptr: torch.Tensor,
632	    kv_indices: torch.Tensor,
633	    kv_last_page_len: torch.Tensor,
634	) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
635	    """PyTorch reference implementation for sparse_page_table conversion.
636	
637	    This is the reference implementation used for testing and verification.
638	    It is NOT CUDA graph compatible due to intermediate allocations.
639	
640	    Args:
641	        sparse_page_table: [sparse_bs, max_sparse_tokens] - Valid entries at start
642	        cache_seqlens: [sparse_bs] - Number of valid entries per row
643	        kv_indptr: Pre-allocated [sparse_bs + 1] buffer for output
644	        kv_indices: Pre-allocated [sparse_bs * max_sparse_tokens] buffer for output
645	        kv_last_page_len: Pre-allocated [sparse_bs] buffer for output
646	
647	    Returns:
648	        Tuple of (kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_last_page_len) - modified in-place
649	    """
650	    sparse_bs = cache_seqlens.shape[0]
651	
652	    # Compute cumulative sum for kv_indptr
653	    kv_indptr[0] = 0
654	    kv_indptr[1:] = torch.cumsum(cache_seqlens, dim=0)
655	
656	    # Flatten sparse_page_table based on cache_seqlens
657	    idx = 0
658	    for i in range(sparse_bs):
659	        num_valid = cache_seqlens[i].item()
660	        if num_valid > 0:
661	            kv_indices[idx : idx + num_valid] = sparse_page_table[i, :num_valid]
662	            idx += num_valid
663	
664	    # Fill kv_last_page_len with ones
665	    kv_last_page_len.fill_(1)
666	
667	    return kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_last_page_len
668	
669	
670	# ============================================================================
671	# Unified Interface
672	# ============================================================================
673	
674	
675	def convert_sparse_page_table_to_flashinfer(
676	    sparse_page_table: torch.Tensor,
677	    cache_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
678	    kv_indptr: torch.Tensor,
679	    kv_indices: torch.Tensor,
680	    kv_last_page_len: torch.Tensor,
681	) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
682	    """Convert sparse_page_table to FlashInfer format.
683	
684	    This is the main entry point that selects between PyTorch reference
685	    implementation and Triton kernel based on USE_TRITON_KERNEL env var.
686	
687	    Args:
688	        sparse_page_table: [sparse_bs, max_sparse_tokens] - Valid entries at start
689	        cache_seqlens: [sparse_bs] - Number of valid entries per row
690	        kv_indptr: Pre-allocated [sparse_bs + 1] buffer for output
691	        kv_indices: Pre-allocated [sparse_bs * max_sparse_tokens] buffer for output
692	        kv_last_page_len: Pre-allocated [sparse_bs] buffer for output
693	
694	    Returns:
695	        Tuple of (kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_last_page_len) - modified in-place
696	
697	    """
698	    if True:
699	        return convert_sparse_to_flashinfer_two_kernel(
700	            sparse_page_table,
701	            cache_seqlens,
702	            kv_indptr,
703	            kv_indices,
704	            kv_last_page_len,
705	        )
706	    else:
707	        return convert_sparse_to_flashinfer_pytorch(
708	            sparse_page_table,
709	            cache_seqlens,
710	            kv_indptr,
711	            kv_indices,
712	            kv_last_page_len,
713	        )
714
