154	// S1 scaffolding entry point.
155	//
156	// Inputs:
157	//   A          (M, K/2)        FP4 packed activations
158	//   B          (N, K/2)        FP4 packed weight rows; N = 2 * intermediate
159	//                              (= "full" gate_up_proj output dim before SwiGLU)
160	//   A_scale    SF buffer       per-block ue4m3
161	//   B_scale    SF buffer       per-block ue4m3
162	//   global_sf  scalar          fp32
163	//   n_out      int             = N / 2 (post-SwiGLU output dim)
164	//
165	// Outputs:
166	//   D          (M, N_out/2)    FP4 packed (post-SwiGLU shape)
167	//   D_scale    SFD buffer      ue4m3 for cute::make_shape(M, N_out, K, 1)
168	//
169	// S1 semantics: the kernel still uses LinCombBlockScaleFactor (no act),
170	// problem_shape passes N_out, weight B passes the first N_out rows only
171	// (caller slices). Numerically this just computes the first half of the
172	// original gate_up GEMM — but build, can_implement, output layout descriptors
173	// all match what S2 will need when the SwiGLU EVT visitor lands.
174	std::vector<torch::Tensor> gate_up_swiglu_fp4_scaffold(
175	    torch::Tensor A,
176	    torch::Tensor B,
177	    torch::Tensor A_scale,
178	    torch::Tensor B_scale,
179	    torch::Tensor global_scale,
180	    int64_t n_out) {
181	  TORCH_CHECK(A.is_cuda() && B.is_cuda() && A_scale.is_cuda() && B_scale.is_cuda());
182	  TORCH_CHECK(A.scalar_type() == torch::kUInt8);
183	  TORCH_CHECK(B.scalar_type() == torch::kUInt8);
184	  TORCH_CHECK(A.dim() == 2 && B.dim() == 2);
185	  int64_t m = A.size(0);
186	  int64_t k_packed = A.size(1);
187	  int64_t k = k_packed * 2;
188	  // For S1: caller pre-slices B to (n_out, k_packed) since EVT visitor isn't
189	  // wired yet. S2 will accept B of shape (2*n_out, k_packed) and pair-reduce
190	  // inside the epilogue.
191	  TORCH_CHECK(B.size(0) == n_out && B.size(1) == k_packed,
192	              "S1 scaffold: B must be (n_out, k_packed); n_out=", n_out,
193	              " got B.shape=", B.sizes());
194	  TORCH_CHECK(n_out % 16 == 0);
195	
196	  auto out = torch::empty({m, n_out / 2}, A.options());
197	  using OutputConfig = cutlass::detail::Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig<16>;
198	  auto sfd_layout = OutputConfig::tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(cute::make_shape(
199	      static_cast<int>(m), static_cast<int>(n_out), static_cast<int>(k), 1));
200	  int64_t sfd_bytes = cute::cosize(sfd_layout);
201	  auto out_scale = torch::empty(
202	      {sfd_bytes},
203	      torch::TensorOptions().device(A.device()).dtype(torch::kUInt8));
204	
205	  using Gemm = typename Fp4BlockscaleEpilogueGemm<128, 128, 128>::Gemm;
206	  run_gemm<Gemm>(out, out_scale, A, B, A_scale, B_scale, global_scale, m, n_out, k);
207	  return {out, out_scale};
208	}
209	
210	int64_t required_sfd_bytes_for_out(int64_t m, int64_t n_out, int64_t k) {
211	  using OutputConfig = cutlass::detail::Sm1xxBlockScaledOutputConfig<16>;
212	  auto sfd_layout = OutputConfig::tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(cute::make_shape(
213	      static_cast<int>(m), static_cast<int>(n_out), static_cast<int>(k), 1));
214	  return cute::cosize(sfd_layout);
215	}

> AGENT

Critical finding: cute_dsl runs MMA at FULL N (`mma_tiler[1]`, weight is `[NxK]` interleaved), and the **C tiler is N/2**. The MMA produces full-N accumulator in tmem; the epilogue then iterates subtiles in pairs (up, gate) at granularity 64, reduces each pair to one output tile of size 64 N, halving the C-side store. The N halving lives entirely in the *C smem layout / epilogue subtile iteration*, not in the GEMM problem shape.

3333	        :rtype: bool
3334	        """
3335	        is_valid = True
3336	
3337	        # Skip invalid mma tile shape
3338	        if mma_tiler_mn[0] not in (128, 256):
3339	            is_valid = False
3340	        # Skip invalid mma tile n
3341	        # SwiGlu Fusion requires even epi_tile counts,
3342	        # based on epi_tile_n = 64, only mma_tiler_n = 128 and 256 are supported
3343	        if mma_tiler_mn[1] not in (128, 256):
3344	            is_valid = False
3345	
3346	        # Skip illegal cluster shape
3347	        if (mma_tiler_mn[0] // cluster_shape_mn[0]) != 128:
3348	            is_valid = False
3349	
3350	        if (
3351	            cluster_shape_mn[0] * cluster_shape_mn[1] > 16
3352	            or cluster_shape_mn[0] <= 0
3353	            or cluster_shape_mn[1] <= 0
3354	            # Special cluster shape check for scale factor multicasts.
3355	            # Due to limited size of scale factors, we can't multicast among more than 4 CTAs.
3356	            or cluster_shape_mn[0] > 4
3357	            or cluster_shape_mn[1] > 4
3358	            or not is_power_of_2(cluster_shape_mn[0])
3359	            or not is_power_of_2(cluster_shape_mn[1])
3360	        ):
3361	            is_valid = False
3362	
3363	        # We only support cluster shape n = 1 for now
3364	        # TODO: Support cluster shape n > 1
3365	        if cluster_shape_mn[1] != 1:
3366	            is_valid = False
3367	        return is_valid

222	      /*
223	      Accumulator fragments are distributed across quads in different warps.
224	      For SFVector = 16, we have:
225	
226	         8 elements          8 elements       8 elements          8 elements
227	      <----------------><-----------------><-----------------><----------------->
228	        Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0
229	        Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1
230	        ...                ...                ...                ...
231	        Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7
232	        Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0
233	        Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1
234	        ...                ...                ...                ...
235	        Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7
236	
237	        <same pattern for warps 1 and 5 for the next set of 16 rows>
238	        <same pattern for warps 2 and 6 for the next set of 16 rows>
239	        <same pattern for warps 3 and 7 for the next set of 16 rows>
240	
241	      In this case, row-wise scale factors are cooperatively reduced across 4
242	      threads from 1 quad in 1 warp. Each quad computes its own, local absolute
243	      maximum without communicating with other warps through shared memory.
244	
245	      For SFVector = 32, we have:
246	         8 elements        8 elements         8 elements         8 elements
247	      <----------------><-----------------><-----------------><----------------->
248	        Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0      Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0
249	        Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1      Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1
250	        ...                ...                ...                ...
251	        Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7      Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7
252	        Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0      Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0
253	        Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1      Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1
254	        ...                ...                ...                ...
255	        Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7      Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7
256	
257	        <same pattern for warps 1 and 5 for the next set of 16 rows>
258	        <same pattern for warps 2 and 6 for the next set of 16 rows>
259	        <same pattern for warps 3 and 7 for the next set of 16 rows>
260	
261	      For SFVector = 64, we have:
262	          8 elements        8 elements         8 elements         8 elements
263	      <----------------><-----------------><-----------------><----------------->
264	        Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 2 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0      Warp 6 Quad 0
265	        Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 2 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1      Warp 6 Quad 1
266	        ...                ...                ...                ...
267	        Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 2 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7      Warp 6 Quad 7
268	        Warp 0 Quad 0      Warp 2 Quad 0      Warp 4 Quad 0      Warp 6 Quad 0
269	        Warp 0 Quad 1      Warp 2 Quad 1      Warp 4 Quad 1      Warp 6 Quad 1
270	        ...                ...                ...                ...
271	        Warp 0 Quad 7      Warp 2 Quad 7      Warp 4 Quad 7      Warp 6 Quad 7
272	
273	        <same pattern for warps 1, 3, 5 and 7 for the next set of 16 rows>
274	
275	      Thus, rowwise scale factors are cooperatively reduced across 8 threads
276	      from two quads in two warps. Each quad first computes its own, local
277	      absolute maximum and then shares this with the corresponding quad in the
278	      other warp. In this case, a reduction through shared memory is needed.
279	
280	      For a non-cooperative epilogue (in which each warpgroup computes a
281	      separate tile), the pattern is the same as that above, except that warps 0
282	      and 2 are in the same row, and 1 and 3 are in the same row, and warps 4-7
283	      are not included.
284	      */

Now I understand the EVT structure: `Sm90EVT<RowStore, LinearCombination>` — `RowStore.reduce()` writes the SFD; the parent EVT pipes `visit_results = tRS_rCompute_frg` (which now lives in the visitor's local registers) into the smem store path (sm90 line 884-891). The smem store is the actual D path.

Now I see exactly what the GMEM/store path uses. The N dimension of D is wired through `make_shape(M, N, L)` from problem_shape (line 571), the `EpilogueTile`, and `CtaTileMNK`. The `gD_epi` shape is `(EPI_TILE_M, EPI_TILE_N, EPI_M, EPI_N)` — these dimensions come from `problem.N / CtaTileMNK.N` and `CtaTileMNK.N / EpilogueTile.N`.

FragmentSize=4 confirmed. Now I have all the info I need. Let me double-check one thing — what does `tRS_rCompute_frg` look like? It's `recast<Array<RegisterElementD, 4>>(tRS_rCompute)` where `tRS_rCompute` has layout `tRS_rD_layout = take<0,3>(thread_r2s.partition_S(sD_epi))` i.e. `(R2S, R2S_M, R2S_N)`. So `tRS_rCompute_frg` shape is `(R2S/4, R2S_M, R2S_N)` with `Array<f32,4>` elements.

Looking back at the visitor's reduce(): `visit_results(0, row, acc_frag_start_for_sf + i)` — index `0` is the V-mode (R2S inner), `row` indexes R2S_M, third index iterates over R2S_N. The 4 elements of Array (acc_frag_row=0,1; col=0,1) are the same MMA 16x8 quad fragment.

Crucially: `tRS_rD_layout` is constructed from `thread_r2s.partition_S(sD_epi)`, where `sD_epi` has `EpilogueTile` shape `(EPI_TILE_M, EPI_TILE_N)`. So the **fragment's per-thread N footprint = EPI_TILE_N / num_threads_per_n**. The outer epi_n loop iterates `CTA_N / EPI_TILE_N` times, and each iteration's `visit_results` covers `EPI_TILE_N` cols.

# Design Report: sm120 NVFP4 GEMM + SwiGLU Pair-Fold Epilogue

## 1. How cute_dsl sm_100 reference halves N

`/opt/SGLang-MiniCPM-SALA/sglang_minicpm_sala_env/lib/python3.10/site-packages/flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/blackwell/blockscaled_contiguous_gather_grouped_gemm_swiglu_fusion.py`

- B is passed at **full N**: `b = cute.make_tensor(b_ptr, layout=...(n, k, l)...)` (line 3528–3529). MMA runs at full N. `mma_tiler[1] = mma_inst_shape_mn[1]` (line 578).
- C is **half N**: `interm_size = n // 2` (line 3523); `c = ...(m, interm_size, 1)...` (line 3541–3543). `c_sf` similarly halved (line 3544–3550).
- Halving is in **a separate C tiler** `mma_tiler_c` (lines 594–598): `mma_tiler_c[1] = mma_inst_shape_mn[1] // 2`. Likewise `cta_tile_shape_mnk_c[1] = cta_tile_shape_mnk[1] // 2` (line 620).
- Inside the epilogue (line 2562–2582): subtiles are iterated in **pairs** of 64 columns: `subtile_idx in range(0, subtile_cnt, 2)`; per iteration loads tmem subtile `2*i` as "up" and `2*i+1` as "gate", computes SwiGLU in register, stores **one** output subtile of width 64 to a C smem buffer sized for `mma_tiler_c[1]`. Output SF tensor is indexed at the halved coord `epi_tile_cnt[1] + real_subtile_idx` (line 2679).
- Constraint: pair-fold granularity = `epi_tile[1] = 64`; valid `mma_tiler_n in {128, 256}` (line 3343); even epi_tile count required (line 3341).

**Implication for sm120**: cute_dsl uses the **two-tiler** approach (full-N MMA tiler vs. half-N C/D tiler) with pair-granularity = `epi_tile_n` (64), not granularity 2. sm120 CUTLASS C++ does not expose a separate `MmaTilerC` parameter — the sm90 epilogue derives `gD_epi` directly from `problem_shape.N` and `CtaTileMNK`. So we cannot literally copy the cute_dsl strategy without forking the collective epilogue.

## 2. Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStore reduce() lines that change

`/user_4813494d/.cache/uv/archive-v0/Ed0N-SHf_T2rFs9wuYc5u/deep_gemm/include/cutlass/epilogue/fusion/sm120_visitor_store_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`

The reduce body iterates SFs over `tC_rSFD_flt` (line 320), reads pairs of accumulator slots `acc_frag[acc_frag_row]`, `acc_frag[acc_frag_row + 1]` (lines 338–339), and writes them back at the same positions after scaling (lines 421–422).

For **pair-fold inside reduce()**, the surgical edits are:

| Original | Replace with |
|---|---|
| L301: `AccFragsPerSF = SFVecSize / (ColsPerThreadAccFrag * NumThreadsPerQuad * WarpsPerSF)` | `AccFragsPerSF_in = SFVecSize / (1 * NumThreadsPerQuad * WarpsPerSF)` (double — each output SF still covers SFVecSize *output* elems; in input domain those occupy 2× the cols, but we still produce only **1 output element per pair**, i.e., per acc_frag the effective ColsPerOutFrag = 1) |
| L302–303 static_assert | `size<2>(visit_results) % AccFragsPerSF_in == 0` and `size<2>(visit_results) % 2 == 0` |
| L336–340 amax loop | replace `amax_op(amax, acc_frg[acc_frag_row])` with `amax_op(amax, swiglu(acc_frg[acc_frag_row + 0], acc_frg_pair[acc_frag_row + 0]))` — see Strategy A below |
| L418–423 scale-write loop | rewrite to (a) compute fused value `out = swiglu(g, u) * acc_scale`, (b) store **into the lower half** of `visit_results`, (c) zero/keep upper half (it gets discarded by the store callback) |

Critically the SF generation rate **does not change** in count if you also halve the SFD layout — output has N/2 cols, each SF covers SFVecSize=16 of those, so each thread still emits the same number of SFs. The shfl_xor pattern (L348–352, L370–376) for amax across quads is unchanged — pair-mate is in the same thread's fragment (positions [0,1] vs [2,3] of `acc_frag`).

**Pair-mate location** confirmed in user prompt: with B permuted so adjacent rows alternate (g, u), the per-thread fragment of size 4 = `{frag[0]=g_i_row0, frag[1]=u_i_row0, frag[2]=g_i_row1, frag[3]=u_i_row1}` because `ColsPerThreadAccFrag=2` and `RowsPerThreadAccFrag=2` — the two cols of one MMA quad fragment are adjacent N — exactly the (g, u) pair. So `swiglu(frag[0], frag[1])` and `swiglu(frag[2], frag[3])` give the two output values for that row-pair, with **zero shuffle**.

## 3. Where visit_results actually becomes a GMEM store

`/user_4813494d/.cache/uv/archive-v0/Ed0N-SHf_T2rFs9wuYc5u/deep_gemm/include/cutlass/epilogue/collective/sm90_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`

The reduce() callback only modifies `tRS_rCompute_frg` in-register and writes SFD to GMEM directly. The D path is:
- L871–872: `cst_callbacks.reduce(..., tRS_rCompute_frg)` (the visitor mutates it in place).
- L884–887: NumericArrayConverter to ElementD (FP4 packing).
- L891: `copy(tiled_r2s, tRS_rD, tRS_sD(...))` — register→smem.
- L734–745, L900: `tma_store_fn(epi_m, epi_n)` → `copy(params.tma_store_d, bSG_sD(...), bSG_gD(_,_,_,epi_m,epi_n))`.

`bSG_gD` partitioning (L646) and `gD_epi = flat_divide(gD, EpilogueTile{})` (L576) both come from `gD = local_tile(mD, take<0,2>(CtaTileMNK{}), coord_shape)` (L573) and `mD = ...get_tma_tensor(make_shape(M,N,L))` (L571) where N = `problem.N`. The TMA descriptor for D is built at `CollectiveBuilder` time from `problem.N` × `LayoutD`.

So **N halving in the GMEM/TMA store path requires** that either (a) the kernel sees `problem.N = N_half` (and we hide the 2× weight rows in the mainloop), or (b) we customize `CollectiveEpilogue` and `tma_store_d` so problem.N (mainloop) ≠ D.N (epilogue).

## 4. Recommended strategy: **C+A hybrid** — call it **Strategy F**

Strategy A pure ("MMA full-N, compress in store") requires writing a custom Sm120 collective epilogue that decouples MMA-N from D-N — too invasive for S2. Strategy B is wrong (drops half the weight). Strategy C alone (LayoutB stride trick) is fragile and likely breaks TMA descriptor assumptions for B. Strategy D defeats the BW savings.

**Strategy F (recommended for S2 PoC)**:

1. **Set `problem.N = N_half`** so the entire collective epilogue (gD, sD, TMA store_d, SFD layout) is half-sized — **no epilogue collective fork needed**.
2. **Double-stride trick on the MMA, in K only** — at GMEM-tile level, swap from "load B[n, k]" to "load B[2n, k] and B[2n+1, k] in adjacent K-tiles, accumulate into adjacent N slots of the same MMA fragment". This is hard.

Actually no — Strategy F is too clever. Let me reconsider.

**Simplest viable S2 (revised recommendation): Strategy A with custom collective epilogue dimensions, but use `problem.N = N_full` and customize ONLY the SFD layout + a thin store wrapper**:

Look again at what's hard-wired by `problem.N`:
- TMA descriptor for D (built in `CollectiveEpilogue` constructor)
- `mD_mn = make_shape(M, N, L)` (sm90 line 571)
- SFD `tile_atom_to_shape_SFD(problem_shape_mnkl)`

All three are computed at host-side from problem_shape. If we set `problem.N = N_full`, we get a full-N D buffer and full-N SFD — the BW win is lost.

**Real simplest viable S2 — Strategy G**: set `problem.N = N_half`, run MMA at N_half, and **pre-permute weight so the (g,u) pair is along K, not N**. I.e.: instead of B having interleaved rows, B has rows `b_i = concat(gate_row_i, up_row_i)` along K and the GEMM computes `Y[i, j] = sum_k a[i, k] * (gate[j, k] + up[j, k])` — NO. That's the wrong math.

OK let me actually think clearly. SwiGLU requires **two separate dot products** per output: `Y_g = a · g`, `Y_u = a · u`, then `out = silu(Y_g) * Y_u`. You cannot fuse them into one dot product. So MMA *must* produce both, the question is just where they live spatially.

**Therefore the only viable answer is the cute_dsl pattern**: MMA at full N, output at half N, with a custom collective epilogue that knows the C/D tiler is half the MMA N tiler.

### Final recommendation for S2 PoC

**Strategy H (the realistic answer)**: do not modify the visitor's `reduce()` first. Instead:

**Stage S2a (the genuinely-simplest PoC, ~50 LOC, no CUTLASS template surgery)**: implement Strategy D (full-N FP4 quantize then a separate Triton/CUDA pair-fold + re-quantize kernel). This validates the **math + permuted-weight layout + reference parity** without touching CUTLASS. Cost: lose BW. Value: provides a known-good numerical reference for S2b and unblocks Eagle/Marlin integration testing.

**Stage S2b (true fused, ~250 LOC)**: fork `Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStore` into `Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStoreSwiGLUFold` (same file, sibling struct), and write a thin `Sm120SwiGLUFusedCollectiveEpilogue` that:
- Takes problem_shape with `N_full` for mainloop sizing but exposes `N_half` for `gD`/`sD`/`tma_store_d`/SFD.
- Constructs `gD_epi` from `local_tile(mD_half, (CTA_M, CTA_N/2), ...)` while `gAcc` still comes from full-N mainloop.
- Iterates the epilogue loop with `epi_n` going `0..size<3>(gD_epi)` (half count), and the visitor sees `tRS_rAcc_frg_mn` indexed by **adjacent pairs of MMA N tiles**.

This **is** the C++ port of `mma_tiler_c[1] = mma_tiler[1] // 2` from cute_dsl.

## 5. Code sketch (S2b, the fused path)

```cpp
// 1. New visitor with pair-fold reduce()
template <int SFVecSize, class EpilogueTile, class CtaTileShapeMNK,
          int FragmentSize, class ElementOutput, class ElementCompute,
          class ElementBlockScaleFactor>
struct Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStoreSwiGLUFold {
  // Identical Arguments/Params/SharedStorage to Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStore
  // visit() still passthrough — work happens in reduce()

  template <class SmemT, class SyncFn, class VTensor>
  CUTLASS_DEVICE void reduce(SmemT&& smem, SyncFn const& sync, int epi_m,
                             int epi_n, bool is_last, VTensor visit_results) {
    static constexpr int ColsPerThreadAccFrag = 2;  // 2 N cols per quad frag
    static constexpr int RowsPerThreadAccFrag = 2;
    static constexpr int NumThreadsPerQuad = 4;
    constexpr int WarpsPerSF = SFVecSize / 16;
    // Each output SF covers SFVecSize output cols == 2*SFVecSize input cols.
    // Per-thread input-col coverage doubles -> 2x AccFragsPerSF:
    constexpr int AccFragsPerSF =
        (SFVecSize * 2) / (ColsPerThreadAccFrag * NumThreadsPerQuad * WarpsPerSF);
    static_assert(size<2>(visit_results) % AccFragsPerSF == 0);

    for (int sf_id = 0; sf_id < size(tC_rSFD_flt); ++sf_id) {
      // ... unchanged coord decoding ...
      ElementCompute amax{0};
      auto acc_frag_row = row_in_acc * RowsPerThreadAccFrag;
      auto acc_frag_start_for_sf = sf * AccFragsPerSF;
      for (int i = 0; i < AccFragsPerSF; ++i) {
        auto& f = visit_results(0, row, acc_frag_start_for_sf + i);
        // Pair-fold: positions [0]=g0,[1]=u0  -> y0
        //            positions [2]=g1,[3]=u1  -> y1
        ElementCompute y_lo = f[acc_frag_row + 0] * f[acc_frag_row + 1];
        ElementCompute y_hi = f[acc_frag_row + 0] * f[acc_frag_row + 1]; // adjust
        // (S2 PoC: identity g*u; replace with silu(g)*u later)
        amax = amax_op(amax, y_lo);
        amax = amax_op(amax, y_hi);
        // Stash fused values back into f[0],f[1] (output domain)
        f[0] = y_lo; f[1] = y_hi;
      }
      // ... unchanged shfl_xor + cross-warp amax reduce ...
      // Write SFD as before (only difference: SFD is sized for N_half via
      // problem_shape passed at host).
      // ... unchanged scale-write loop — but loop body now stores back into
      //     f[0..1] only (f[2..3] are dead garbage).
    }
    // Unchanged write_sf gate and copy_aligned.
  }
};

// 2. Fork the CollectiveEpilogue so D-side uses N_half but mainloop sees N_full.
// Simplest: subclass / wrap the sm90 collective with a host-side trick.
// Two-problem-shape approach in prepare_args:
//   - mainloop is sized by (M, N_full, K, L)
//   - epilogue's gD/sD/tma_store_d/SFD are sized by (M, N_half, K, L)
//   - this requires forking the collective builder OR a manual GemmKernel
//     instantiation where the CollectiveEpilogue is constructed with a
//     reduced "problem shape" while CollectiveMainloop holds full N.

// 3. fusion::FusionCallbacks specialization for a new LinCombSwiGLUFoldBSF op
//    that wires Sm90EVT<Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStoreSwiGLUFold<...>,
//                       Sm90LinearCombination<...>>.
```

The fork point is `CollectiveBuilder` lines 491–501 in `sm120_builder.inl`. The cleanest implementation is to write a manual `CollectiveEpilogue` template (bypass the builder) where you pass two different `CtaTileMNK` sizes: a "mainloop tile" with N=128 and an "epilogue tile" with N=64. Then `gD`/`sD`/`tma_store_d` are built from the epilogue tile. Mainloop accumulator stays sized to N=128; visitor sees `tRS_rAcc_frg` of double N-extent vs. `tRS_rD_frg`, and the pair-fold drops the second half.

## 6. Pitfalls

1. **Builder will reject inconsistent tile sizes.** `Sm120TmaBuilderImpl` derives `EpilogueTile_MN` from `TileShape_MNK` and asserts `EpilogueTile_MN | CtaTileMNK`. You must hand-roll the epilogue template instantiation, not use `CollectiveBuilder`.
2. **SmemD swizzle atom is sized by EpilogueTile.** If epilogue tile N changes from 128→64, the smem swizzle (`sm120_get_epilogue_smem_swizzle_layout_atom`, sm120_builder.inl L375) regenerates; make sure your hand-rolled version uses the half-N tile.
3. **`Sm90LinearCombination::visit()` returns the binary op result of size FragmentSize=4.** Your pair-fold reduces 4 acc lanes to 2 output lanes — but `tRS_rCompute_frg` is shaped `(FragmentSize=4, ..., R2S_N)`. Either: (a) keep FragmentSize=4 and waste-write the upper half (then the store callback's `tiled_r2s` will write garbage to smem positions that **must not** be TMA'd — needs predication), or (b) introduce a half-sized `tRS_rCompute_half_frg` view and a custom `tiled_r2s` that copies only the lower 2 lanes per fragment.
4. **AccFragsPerSF doubles** (output SF covers same #output cols but 2× input MMA cols). Verify `size<2>(visit_results) % AccFragsPerSF == 0` does not regress.
5. **Norm constant & amax over FUSED values, not raw acc.** Apply `silu(g)*u` first, then amax — the existing reduce() does amax over raw acc; you must move the fused-compute *before* amax. This is shown in cute_dsl line 2664 (compute) → line 2696 (amax over `tCompute`).
6. **SiLU numerical accuracy.** cute_dsl uses `exp2(-x*log2e)` + `rcp_approx` (line 2624–2639). Approximate, fastmath. PoC can start with `silu(x) = x / (1 + __expf(-x))`; tighten later.
7. **Norm constant double-application.** `LinCombBlockScaleFactor` multiplies by `alpha` in `Sm90LinearCombination::visit()` and again uses `norm_constant` in `Sm120BlockScaleFactorRowStore`. With pair-fold, `silu(alpha*g) * (alpha*u)` is what cute_dsl does (lines 2658–2666). Make sure alpha is applied **before** silu, not after.
8. **TMA store size mismatch.** TMA D descriptor stride is set from `problem.N` at kernel init. If you cheat and only call TMA with N_half elements per tile, the descriptor must be built for an N_half tensor — meaning user-side allocation, problem_shape, and SFD layout **must** be N_half. The output buffer in `prepare_args` must be sized `(M, N_half/2 bytes)`. This is already correct in the scaffold.
9. **`MmaNPerEpiN` branch (sm90 line 824).** If your hand-rolled epilogue keeps `EpilogueTile.N=64` but `MmaTile.N=128`, the `epi_tile_m * epi_tile_n > mma_tile_m * mma_tile_n` path triggers; you get an inner mma loop iterating `MmaNPerEpiN=2` times — exactly the pair-iteration. **This is the natural insertion point**: when `MmaNPerEpiN==2`, the visitor visit() is called twice per epi_n, with `mma_n_in_epi=0` (gate) and `mma_n_in_epi=1` (up). Pair-fold can be done in `visit()` by stateful accumulation across these two calls instead of inside `reduce()`. **This is actually the cleanest implementation path** and avoids most of the visitor surgery.

### Revised final recommendation

Use the **`MmaNPerEpiN==2` natural pair-iteration** at sm90_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:830–843 (Strategy I). Concretely: keep CUTLASS builder happy by setting `CtaTileMNK = (CTA_M, CTA_N=128, CTA_K)` and `EpilogueTile = (EPI_M, EPI_N=64)`. With problem.N = N_half, mainloop produces full-N fragments (... no, mainloop is also driven by CtaTileMNK.N=128). To get the **full-N MMA but half-N epilogue**, the EpilogueTile alone isn't enough — you still need decoupled tilers, which means the hand-rolled CollectiveEpilogue.

**The honest minimum complexity for true fused S2 is ~300 LOC: a fork of the visitor (~100), a fork of `Sm120TmaBuilderImpl` to decouple MMA-N from D-N (~150), new `FusionCallbacks` specialization (~50).** Start with **S2a (Strategy D)** to lock down the math, then S2b.

### Key file references for the implementer

- Visitor to fork: `sm120_visitor_store_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:60-510` (reduce body `:219-450`)
- Where visit_results becomes D smem store: `sm90_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:884-891`
- TMA D store call: `sm90_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:734-745`

## 背景

我们当前的 stack:

当前 stage2 sparse FA 路径:

- 实测 4.80s / 16.5% wall (524K prefill, 512 calls, 9.37ms/call)

- 每 chunk 8 sparse layer × 64 chunks = 512 calls

## 调查目标

判断能否将 stage2 sparse FA 切到 `backend="fa3"`,且**不破坏当前 venv 其他组件**（不动 PyTorch、不动 sgl-kernel、不替换 .so）。

## 调查任务

### 1. FA3 backend 在 sm120 的硬件支持

- 看 `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper.plan/begin_forward/forward` 内 `backend="fa3"` 路径需要的 module — 比如 `gen_batch_prefill_attention_sm90_module()` 或其他 sm-specific gen 函数。这些是 JIT compile (运行时 build) 还是 prebuilt？

### 2. JIT vs prebuilt

  (b) JIT compile sm90 module, runtime IMA
  (c) Silent fallback to fa2

583	    pattern used by ``is_sm100a_supported`` (``major == 10``).
584

587	    """

592	    return version_at_least(torch.version.cuda, min_cuda)

166	def make_hashable_cache(func):
167	    """
168	    Decorator that converts unhashable arguments (like lists) to hashable ones (tuples)
169	    before applying functools.cache.
170	    """
171	
172	    @functools.cache
173	    def cached_wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
174	        return func(*args, **kwargs)
175	
176	    @functools.wraps(func)
177	    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
178	        # Convert unhashable arguments to hashable ones
179	        hashable_args = []
180	        for arg in args:
181	            if isinstance(arg, list):
182	                hashable_args.append(tuple(arg))
183	            else:
184	                hashable_args.append(arg)
185	
186	        hashable_kwargs = {}
187	        for key, value in kwargs.items():
188	            if isinstance(value, list):
189	                hashable_kwargs[key] = tuple(value)
190	            else:
191	                hashable_kwargs[key] = value
192	
193	        return cached_wrapper(*hashable_args, **hashable_kwargs)
194	
195	    return wrapper
196

## FlashAttention 3 and SM120 Support

FlashAttention-4 will not run on the NVIDIA RTX 5090 (SM120, "desktop Blackwell") and despite sharing the "Blackwell" brand with data center GPUs like the B200 (SM100), the RTX 5090 uses a fundamentally different tensor core architecture.

The core issue is architectural: SM120 uses the older HMMA instruction family (the same register-to-register MMA approach used since Volta/Ampere) and the TMEM hardware is physically absent from the GB202 die. This is not a software lock, not a fuse bit, and not a toolchain oversight — it is a silicon-level architectural difference.

## Recommended Alternative

For RTX 5090 users: FlashAttention-2 via Triton (the default flex_attention backend) is your best available attention kernel. It is still fast — the 5090 has excellent bandwidth and clock speeds — but it will not benefit from FA4's tensor-memory-based optimizations.

## RTX 6000D Support

There are references to compatibility questions regarding the RTX 6000 Blackwell (RTX 6000D/Pro), but the search results don't provide definitive information about FlashAttention 3 support for that card specifically, though it appears to face similar SM120 architectural limitations.

**Attention Kernel Support:**
The backend selector only checks for SM90, so SM120 falls through to generic FA2 (Ampere-level), even though SM120-specific FMHA_V2 kernels exist.

The search results indicate that FlashInfer has significant compatibility challenges with consumer Blackwell (SM120) GPUs, particularly regarding advanced attention backends and compute capability detection.

# SM120 Attention Kernels: Status & Wiring Issues

## What Works on SM120

- **XQA decode (MHA)**: Functional via `xqa.py` (supports SM compute versions [9, 10, 12])
- **SM120 GEMM (FP8, FP4)**: Operational through dedicated CUTLASS kernels

## What Doesn't Work

- **FA3 backend**: Not supported—no routing exists for SM120
- **FMHA_V2 SM120 prefill**: Kernels exist but remain ungenerated and unrouted to the runtime
- **XQA decode (MLA, FP8)**: Code exists but reportedly fails per Issue #2166

## Three Critical Wiring Issues

**Issue 1 — FMHA_V2 generation gated by environment variable**
The codebase only generates SM120 FMHA_V2 kernels when `"ENABLE_SM120"` is set. "SM120-specific FMHA_V2 kernels are only generated if the ENABLE_SM120 environment variable is set."

**Issue 2 — Backend selector ignores SM120**
The `determine_attention_backend()` function only checks for SM90a support and defaults everything else to generic FA2, completely bypassing the existing SM120 optimization paths.

**Issue 3 — MLA routing uses FA2 instead of XQA**
The `determine_mla_backend()` function returns FA2 for SM120, despite an existing XQA MLA backend specifically compiled for this architecture (`mla_sm120.cu`).

## No Patches Mentioned
The issue report proposes three fixes but provides no code patches.

# FlashAttention-4 and RTX 5090 (SM120): Deep Investigation Summary

## Why FA4 Cannot Run on RTX 5090

The investigation reveals a **silicon-level architectural difference**, not a software limitation. The RTX 5090 (GB202, SM120) lacks the dedicated tensor memory (TMEM) subsystem that FlashAttention-4 fundamentally requires. Despite sharing the "Blackwell" branding with data center GPUs, SM120 uses an older tensor core design incompatible with FA4's warp-specialized kernels.

### Key Finding
"FlashAttention-4 will not run on the NVIDIA RTX 5090 (SM120, "desktop Blackwell") and no amount of software patching can fix it."

The investigation progressed through multiple layers:
1. **Python-level gatekeepers** blocked SM120 from compilation paths
2. **NVVM MLIR compiler** rejected `tcgen05` instructions (bitmask only covered SM100 family)
3. **ptxas assembler** explicitly rejected `tcgen05` instructions for SM120 targets
4. **SASS disassembly** confirmed the architectural gap

## About FA3

The document does not discuss FlashAttention-3. It focuses exclusively on FA4 incompatibility and notes that "FlashAttention-2 via Triton remains the best available attention kernel for the RTX 5090."

## Architectural Differences: SM100 vs. SM120

| Feature | SM100 (B200/B300) | SM120 (RTX 5090) |
|---------|-------------------|-----------------|
| **Tensor Memory (TMEM)** | Full `UTMA*`/`UTC*` ISA | Absent |
| **MMA Instruction** | `UTCHMMA.2CTA` (TMEM-backed) | `HMMA.16816` (register-backed) |
| **2CTA Clusters** | Supported | Not supported |
| **Warp-Specialized Kernels** | Compatible | Cannot express |

SM120 tensor cores are "architecturally closer to Hopper than to data center Blackwell," using register-to-register MMA operations inherited from Volta rather than TMEM-based computation.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about SM120, wgmma, TMA support, and Blackwell consumer RTX 5090:

## Key Findings:

**WGMMA Instruction Incompatibility with SM120:**

Compiling WGMMA code targeting SM12x produces ptxas error: Instruction 'wgmma.fence' not supported on .target 'sm_120'. SM90a kernels use wgmma instructions that are not compatible with SM120.

**TMA Support on SM120:**

SM12x lacks the TMEM hardware entirely, and therefore does not support the tcgen05 instruction that controls it. However, TMA is used for weights to load input matrices in some Blackwell SM100 kernels.

**Consumer Blackwell (RTX 5090) Differences:**

Consumer Blackwell put new data types on top of the oldest programming model. The tensor core instruction that SM12x actually uses is an extended version of mma.sync, the same instruction family that dates back to Ampere. SM120 (consumer Blackwell) does not have tcgen05 instructions or TMEM — it uses mma.sync.aligned.block_scale instead of tcgen05.mma.

**Hopper vs. Blackwell:**

The Hopper WGMMA instruction has been deprecated on Blackwell. To replace it, Blackwell introduced the tcgen05.mma instruction for MMA.

# FA3 backend 在 sm120 上的非破坏性启用调研

## 1. FA3 backend 在 sm120 的硬件支持

**关键代码路径**：
- `flashinfer/utils.py:543-545` `is_sm90a_supported`: `major == 9 and cuda >= 12.3` — **只接受 Hopper**
- `flashinfer/utils.py:500-509` `determine_attention_backend`: `return "fa3" if is_sm90a_supported(...)` else `"fa2"` — sm120 (major=12) 在 `auto` 模式下**永不**走 fa3
- `flashinfer/utils.py:563-565` `is_sm120a_supported`: `major == 12 and minor == 0 and cuda >= 12.8` — sm120 有独立 gate，但 fa3 路径不查它

**结论**：FlashInfer 0.6.8.post1 **不把 fa3 backend 视为 sm120 的合法目标**。`auto` 在 sm120 上 100% 回落 fa2。

**可信度**：代码 verified。

---

## 2. JIT vs prebuilt — fa3 module 编译路径

**关键代码路径**：
- `flashinfer/jit/attention/modules.py:1619-1694` `gen_batch_prefill_module(backend="fa3", ...)`:
  - 用模板 `batch_prefill_sm90_customize_config.jinja`、`batch_prefill_paged_sm90_kernel_inst.jinja`、`batch_prefill_sm90.cu`
  - **`extra_cuda_cflags=sm90a_nvcc_flags`** (`flashinfer/jit/core.py:127`: `-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a`)
- `flashinfer/jit/attention/modules.py:988-990`: `assert backend in ["fa2", "fa3"]` — 没有 fa3-for-sm120 分支
- 源码 `data/include/flashinfer/attention/hopper/mainloop.cuh:41-42` 用 `cute::SM90_TMA_LOAD/STORE`
- `kernel_traits.cuh:76-110` 用 `cute::GMMA::ss_op_selector / rs_op_selector` (WGMMA 描述符)
- `epilogue.cuh:81-96` 用 `GMMA::Major::K`、`SM90_U32x4_STSM_N`、`SM90_TMA_STORE`

**结论**：fa3 是 JIT 编译（不是 prebuilt cubin），但模板**只产 sm_90a SASS**。源码 include `flashinfer/attention/hopper/*.cuh`，其中**密集使用 SM90 专属 PTX**：WGMMA (`GMMA::*`)、TMA bulk copy (`SM90_TMA_LOAD/STORE`)、Hopper-only 同步原语。

**可信度**：代码 verified。

---

## 3. 强制 `backend="fa3"` 在 sm120 会发生什么

追逻辑（`prefill.py:1485-1634` 构造 → `1976-2001` plan → `get_batch_prefill_module(backend="fa3", ...)` → `gen_batch_prefill_module` → JIT compile）：

1. Python 侧**没有 architecture assert**——`backend="fa3"` 直接绕过 `determine_attention_backend`，没有 raise。
2. `gen_batch_prefill_module` 用 `sm90a_nvcc_flags` 调 nvcc。
3. nvcc/ptxas 在 cu13 (`/usr/local/cuda-13.2`) 上**会成功编译出 sm_90a SASS**（host 不需要 sm_90 GPU 来编译）。
4. 加载 `.so`、`build_and_load()` 成功（cudart 不在 load 时检查 SASS 对当前设备的兼容性）。
5. **第一次 kernel launch**时，runtime 会拿不到 `sm_120` 的 cubin/PTX entry → `cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice` (`error 209: "no kernel image is available for execution on the device"`)。
   - 这正是 Dao-AILab/flash-attention#1638 报的错。
   - **没有 PTX fallback**：`-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a` 不带 `code=compute_90a` PTX，所以 JIT-to-target 也不可行；即便带 PTX，sm_120 ptxas 也会拒绝 `wgmma`/`SM90_TMA_*` 指令（外部确认 `wgmma.fence not supported on .target 'sm_120'`）。

**结论**：强制 fa3 → **运行时崩**（选项 b 的精确变体：JIT compile 成功，第一次 launch IMA / `cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice`）。**不会** silent fallback to fa2。

**可信度**：代码 verified + 外部 issue 交叉确认。

---

## 4. FlashInfer 内其他 backend 在 sm120 的可行性

| Backend | sm120 支持？ | 证据 |
|---|---|---|
| **fa2** | 是（生产路径） | 当前在用 |
| **fa3** | 否（sm_90a only） | §1-3 |
| **cudnn** | 部分 | `cudnn_fmha_gen` 依赖 prebuilt cubin (`gen_cudnn_fmha_module`, `modules.py:1891-1900`)；需 cuDNN 9.x sdpa cubin 含 sm120。我们装的是 cuDNN 9.21，可能含 sm120 sdpa（cuDNN 9.15+ 是我们栈的硬要求），但**只支持 `NHD` layout + `causal=True`**。stage2 sparse 不是 causal-mask，且 mask_mode=0。**不适用**。 |
| **cutlass** | **明确否决** | `prefill.py:159-163`: "CUTLASS FMHA requires SM100a (B200/GB200) or SM110a. SM12x (RTX 5090/DGX Spark) lacks tcgen05 MMA required by this kernel. Use backend='fa2' instead." |
| **trtllm-gen** | sm120 cubin 存在但不适用 | `prefill.py:2004-2009`: trtllm-gen paged KV **强制 causal=True**，sparse stage2 mask_mode=0 → raise NotImplementedError |
| **cute-dsl** | sm120 部分支持，**paged KV not supported** | `prefill.py:1554-1559`: `raise NotImplementedError("cute-dsl backend is not yet supported for paged KV cache.")` |
| **`gen_trtllm_fmha_v2_sm120_module`** | sm120-only，但**仅 DeepSeek-R1 192/128 MLA** | `modules.py:1903-1936`：硬编码 3 个 kernel 文件全部 `192x128`（MLA）；`fmha_v2_prefill_deepseek` `prefill.py:4192` 要求 `query.shape[3] == 192 and key.shape[3] == 192 and value.shape[3] == 128`。**我们是 128/128 GQA，无关**。 |

**结论**：FlashInfer 内 sm120 上**没有**比 fa2 更优的 paged sparse non-causal backend。最有潜力的 `trtllm_fmha_v2_sm120` 是 DeepSeek-MLA 专用。

**可信度**：代码 verified。

---

## 5. 上游 FA3 / FlashAttention 对 Blackwell 的支持

**官方仓库（Dao-AILab/flash-attention）**：
- 最新 release **2.8.3**（2025-08-15），主分支只支持 Ampere/Ada/Hopper（compute capability ≤ 9.0），**无 sm120 wheel**。
- FA3 在 `hopper/` 子目录，beta 状态，**显式 H100/H800 only**。
- Issue #1638（2025-05）/ #1665（2025-05）/ #1810：sm120 + FA3 **未支持**，无 PR 落地。
- FA4 在 sm120 也不可行（缺 TMEM/tcgen05），见 issue #1810 + solatticus gist。

**架构事实（来自 ptxas / gau-nernst 博客 / cutlass#3096 等）**：
| 指令 | SM90 (Hopper) | SM100 (B200) | SM120 (RTX 5090/6000D) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `wgmma` (WGMMA) | yes | deprecated | **NO** (`ptxas: 'wgmma.fence' not supported on .target 'sm_120'`) |
| `cute::SM90_TMA_LOAD/STORE` (TMA via `cp.async.bulk.tensor`) | yes | yes | **partial** (`cp.async.bulk` 存在但无 wgmma 同步原语，FA3 模板不可用) |
| `tcgen05.mma` / TMEM | no | yes | **NO** |
| `mma.sync.aligned.block_scale` (Ampere-style) | no (legacy mma) | yes | **yes**（sm120 唯一的 TC 路径） |

SM120 的张量核**架构上更接近 Ampere**（用 register-backed mma.sync），既没有 SM90 的 WGMMA，也没有 SM100 的 tcgen05/TMEM。**Hopper FA3 kernel 在 sm120 上无法物理执行**——这是 silicon-level 限制，不是 wheel/wiring 问题。

**社区 fork**：无可用 sm120 FA3 port。gau-nernst 博客手写了 sm120 attention，但**只用 Ampere 指令 (`mma.m16n8k16`)**，不是 FA3，且不是 FlashInfer 兼容的 ABI。

**可信度**：代码 verified + 多源 cross-check（CUTLASS issue #3096、FlashInfer issue #2555/#2723、Tri Dao #1638/#1810、solatticus gist、gau-nernst 博客）。

---

## 6. 非破坏性安装路径评估

**flash-attn PyPI 独立装的可行性**：
- `flash-attn 2.8.3` PyPI wheel **不含 sm120 binary**（FA2 path 也没有 sm120 wheel），且只支持 PyTorch ≤2.x ABI（cu118-cu126），与我们 cu130 + PyTorch 2.11 不兼容。
- FA3 不在 PyPI，要从源码 `cd hopper && python setup.py install`，编译时被 `wgmma.fence not supported on sm_120` 顶死。
- **即使装了** `flash-attn`，FlashInfer 的 `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="fa3")` 也**不会**调它——FlashInfer fa3 走自己的 JIT module（`gen_batch_prefill_module(backend="fa3")`），完全独立于 PyPI 的 `flash_attn` 包。两个 fa3 path 是分离的 implementation。

**结论**：装 `flash-attn` 既装不上（编译失败），也不会被 FlashInfer wrapper 使用。**这条路死透**。

**可信度**：代码 verified（FlashInfer JIT 不 import `flash_attn`） + PyPI 文档 verified。

---

## 7. 风险评估总结

### 可行性结论
**在 sm120 (RTX 6000D) 上把 stage2 sparse FA 切到 FlashInfer fa3 backend = 不可行 (P0 blocker, silicon-level)**

### 三条独立的 hard blocker（任何一条单独就足以否决）
1. **Python gate**：`determine_attention_backend` 不返回 fa3；强制 `backend="fa3"` 绕过 gate 后 ⤵
2. **NVCC gencode gate**：fa3 模板用 `sm90a_nvcc_flags`（`compute_90a,sm_90a`），编出的 SASS 在 sm120 上 `cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice`
3. **PTX gate (user_4813494d cause)**：FA3 源码用 `cute::SM90_TMA_LOAD/STORE` + `GMMA::*` (WGMMA)，sm120 silicon **物理上不支持 wgmma** (`ptxas: wgmma.fence not supported on .target 'sm_120'`)

### 替代 attack 推荐（按推荐度排序）

#### A. 否决 — 不要碰
- ~~FlashInfer `backend="fa3"`~~：本调研 P0 否决
- ~~FlashInfer `backend="cutlass"`~~：sm120 缺 tcgen05，prefill.py:159 主动 raise
- ~~FlashInfer `backend="trtllm-gen"`~~：要 causal=True，sparse stage2 mask_mode=0 不匹配
- ~~FlashInfer `backend="cudnn"`~~：要 causal=True
- ~~`gen_trtllm_fmha_v2_sm120_module`~~：DeepSeek-MLA 192/128 专用
- ~~独立装 flash-attn~~：编译失败 + FlashInfer 不会用它

#### B. 仍在 sm120 fa2 框架内可探索（不需要 fa3）
1. **Sweep FA2 CTA_TILE_Q / NUM_MMA_KV** 重编：当前 kernel name `CTA_TILE_Q=16, NUM_MMA_Q=1, NUM_MMA_KV=1, NUM_MMA_D_QK=8, NUM_MMA_D_VO=8`。sparse stage2 是 **decode-style (max_seqlen_q=1)**，tile_q=16 已经接近最小，往大 tile 调优空间很小；但 `NUM_MMA_KV` 可能可以增大改善 KV 吞吐。需要修 FlashInfer C++ 模板（`batch_prefill.cu` jinja）+ JIT 重编。属于 "需要 rebuild FlashInfer" 的 path。
2. **替换为 sgl-kernel / 自研 sm120 sparse attention**（gau-nernst-style Ampere-MMA 手写）：可控性最高，但 engineering 量大，需做 mma.sync + cp.async pipeline。
3. **算法层面减少 stage2 调用数**：当前 8 sparse layer × 64 chunks = 512 calls，9.37ms/call。如果能把 stage2 fuse 多层或多 chunk，或减少 top-K block 数，wall 收益可能 ≫ 单 kernel 替换。
4. **XQA-style decode kernel 复用到 stage2**：FlashInfer 的 XQA 支持 sm120（`xqa.py` 接受 SM ∈ {9,10,12}，issue #2555 确认），stage2 是 decode-style (max_seqlen_q=1)。这是**最有潜力的非破坏性路径**——XQA 是 sm120 native、page_size=1 friendly、kv_heads=2 GQA 兼容。需查 XQA 是否支持 sparse `kv_indices`（而不是 contiguous block_table），如果可以，**这是真正可以攻**的方向。

### 最低破坏性建议
**完全放弃 fa3 attack**，把工程时间投到：
- **优先调研 XQA backend for stage2**（见 B.4，sm120 native，最有希望）
- 次优：FA2 模板 `CTA_TILE_Q` / `NUM_MMA_KV` sweep + JIT rebuild（不动 venv，只新增 JIT cache 目录）

---

## TL;DR

FlashInfer 0.6.8.post1 的 fa3 backend 在 sm120 **三层硬阻塞**：(1) Python 侧 `determine_attention_backend` 只接受 sm90a；(2) JIT 用 `-gencode=arch=compute_90a,code=sm_90a` 编出来的 SASS 在 sm120 launch IMA；(3) 模板源码 (`hopper/*.cuh`) 用 `cute::SM90_TMA_LOAD` + `GMMA::*` (WGMMA)，而 **sm120 silicon 不支持 wgmma**（ptxas 主动拒绝）。这是硅级限制，非 wiring 问题，无任何软件 patch 可解。FlashInfer 其他 sm120 backend (cutlass / trtllm-gen / cudnn / trtllm_fmha_v2_sm120) 全部因 causal-only 或 MLA-specific 不适用 sparse stage2。**推荐放弃 fa3 attack，改攻 XQA backend for stage2**（sm120 native，decode-style 匹配 max_seqlen_q=1，是真正可行的替代路径），或留在 fa2 内做 `CTA_TILE_Q`/`NUM_MMA_KV` 重编 sweep。无任何安装/构建动作执行。

深入调查 FlashInfer 0.6.8.post1 的 **XQA backend** 在 sm120 (NVIDIA RTX 6000D / Blackwell consumer) 上能否替换我们当前的 stage2 sparse FA。这是 OpenBMB/MiniCPM-SALA 长上下文 prefill 优化项目的延续调研。**只调研，不安装/构建/replace .so**。

## 背景

我们当前 stage2 sparse FA 实测 4.80s / 16.5% wall (524K prefill, 512 calls/forward, 9.37ms/call)。当前调用：
- `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper(backend="fa2")` 创建于 `demo-sala/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/minicpm_attention_kernels.py:363`
- nsys kernel: `flashinfer::BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel<KernelTraits<MaskMode=0, CTA_TILE_Q=16, NUM_MMA_Q=1, NUM_MMA_KV=1, NUM_MMA_D_QK=8, NUM_MMA_D_VO=8, NUM_KV_HEADS=1, NUM_WARPS=4>>`
- sparse stage2 实际形态:
  - `max_seqlen_q == 1` per row（decode-style）
  - `MaskMode=0`（无 causal，sparse 选择的 blocks 全 valid）
  - GQA: `num_qo_heads=32`, `num_kv_heads=2`, `head_dim=128`
  - `page_size=1`
  - `kv_indices` 来自 R38-style sparse selection（top-K block indices per row × head_group），非 contiguous
  - 8 sparse layers × 64 chunks = 512 calls per forward
- 前一次调研 (FA3) 结论：sm120 silicon 不支持 WGMMA, FA3 三层硬阻塞

### 4. 实测潜在性能特征

- nsys / docs / issue / PR comments 中是否有 XQA vs fa2 prefill 在 sm120 / sm90 上的对比数据?
- XQA 的 KernelTraits 是否暴露 CTA tile size / num_warps 等参数 sweep?
- 是否有 `gen_xqa_module(...)` 的 JIT generator? 用什么 nvcc flags?

### 5. 替换可行性 + 工程量评估

如果 XQA 兼容 sparse stage2，给出 minimal swap plan:
- 改 `_get_or_create_prefill_wrapper` 创建 XQA wrapper 而非 prefill_wrapper
- 调整 begin_forward / forward 调用签名
- bitwise 等价性测试方式
- 风险：是否破坏 KV pool layout / page_size / 等

### 6. 找到一个 fallback attack

如果 XQA 不兼容 sparse stage2（mask_mode / max_seqlen_q / paged kv layout 任何一个不符），给出最有希望的下一个 attack。可考虑：
- FlashInfer 内**未调研过的其他 sm120 backend** (比如 xqa-like / cute-dsl 的 ragged / 其他 prefill kernel template)
- 手写 sm120 ampere-style mma.sync sparse FA kernel（gau-nernst 类）的工程量
- 完全跳出 FlashInfer 的其他选项

192	    v_cache: torch.Tensor

195	        Data type should match query tensor or be torch.float8_e4m3fn, in which case xqa will run fp8 calculation.

199	        or ``[num_pages, num_kv_heads, page_size, head_dim / 16]`` if :attr:`kv_layout` is ``HND``. Should be the same data type as v_sf_cache. Data type should be torch.uint8.
200	    v_sf_cache: Optional[torch.Tensor]
201	        Optional scale factor cache tensor for the V cache. Use when NVFP4 KV is used. Expected shape is ``[num_pages, page_size, num_kv_heads, head_dim / 16]`` if :attr:`kv_layout` is ``NHD``,
202	        or ``[num_pages, num_kv_heads, page_size, head_dim / 16]`` if :attr:`kv_layout` is ``HND``. Should be the same data type as k_sf_cache. Data type should be torch.uint8.
203	    page_table : torch.Tensor
204	        Page table tensor with shape ``batch_size, nb_pages_per_seq``.
205	        Data type should be torch.int32.
206	        K and V share the same table.
207	    seq_lens : torch.Tensor
208	        Sequence lengths tensor with shape ``[batch_size, beam_width]``.
209	        Data type should be torch.uint32.
210	    output : torch.Tensor
211	        Output tensor with shape that matches the query tensor.
212	        Data type should match query tensor or kv tensor. This tensor will be modified in-place.
213	    workspace_buffer : torch.Tensor

247	        Shape: ``[batch_size, q_seq_len, mask_size_per_row]`` where
248	        ``mask_size_per_row = ((q_seq_len + 31) // 32) * 2``.
249	        Data type should be torch.uint16 (bit-packed format, aligned to 32 bits).
250	
251	    Note
252	    ----
253	    The function automatically infers several parameters from tensor shapes:
254	    - batch_size from q.shape[0]
255	    - num_q_heads from q.shape[-2]
256	    - head_dim from q.shape[-1]
257	    - input_dtype from q.dtype
258	    - kv_cache_dtype from k.dtype

261	    """
262	    # Handle optional parameters
263	    if sm_count is None:

265	
266	    enable_pdl = enable_pdl if enable_pdl is not None else device_support_pdl(q.device)
267	
268	    # Infer parameters from tensors
269	    batch_size = q.shape[0]
270	    num_q_heads = q.shape[-2]
271	    head_dim = q.shape[-1]
272	
273	    # Calculate head_group_ratio
274	    head_group_ratio = num_q_heads // num_kv_heads
275	
276	    # Calculate max_seq_len from page_table and page_size
277	    num_pages_per_seq = page_table.shape[-1]
278	    max_seq_len = num_pages_per_seq * page_size

280	    # Determine if sliding window is used

445	@flashinfer_api
446	def xqa_mla(
447	    q: torch.Tensor,
448	    k_cache: torch.Tensor,
449	    v_cache: torch.Tensor,
450	    page_table: torch.Tensor,
451	    seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
452	    output: torch.Tensor,
453	    workspace_buffer: torch.Tensor,
454	    semaphores: torch.Tensor,
455	    page_size: int,
456	    q_scale: Union[float, torch.Tensor] = 1.0,
457	    kv_scale: Union[float, torch.Tensor] = 1.0,
458	    sm_count: Optional[int] = None,
459	    enable_pdl: Optional[bool] = None,
460	) -> None:
461	    r"""Apply attention with paged KV cache using XQA MLA (Multi-Head Latent Attention) kernel.
462	    Parameters
463	    ----------
464	    q : torch.Tensor
465	        Query tensor with shape ``[batch_size, beam_width, num_q_heads, head_dim]``.
466	        Data type should be torch.float8_e4m3fn.
467	        Now only beam_width 1 is supported.
468	    k_cache: torch.Tensor
469	        Paged K cache tensor with shape ``[total_num_cache_heads, head_dim]``.
470	        Data type should be torch.float8_e4m3fn
471	    v_cache: torch.Tensor
472	        Paged V cache tensor with shape ``[total_num_cache_heads, head_dim]``.
473	        Data type should be torch.float8_e4m3fn
474	    page_table : torch.Tensor
475	        Page table tensor with shape ``batch_size, nb_pages_per_seq``.
476	        Data type should be torch.int32.
477	        K and V share the same table.
478	    seq_lens : torch.Tensor
479	        Sequence lengths tensor with shape ``[batch_size, beam_width]``.
480	        Data type should be torch.uint32.
481	    output : torch.Tensor
482	        Output tensor with shape ``[batch_size, beam_width, num_q_heads, head_dim]``.
483	        Data type should be torch.bfloat16. This tensor will be modified in-place.
484	    workspace_buffer : torch.Tensor
485	        Workspace buffer for temporary computations.
486	        Data type should be torch.uint8.
487	    semaphores : torch.Tensor
488	        Semaphore buffer for synchronization.
489	        Data type should be torch.uint32.
490	    page_size : int
491	        Size of each page in the paged KV cache. Must be one of [16, 32, 64, 128].
492	    q_scale : Union[float, torch.Tensor], default=1.0
493	        Scale factor for query tensor.
494	    kv_scale : Union[float, torch.Tensor], default=1.0
495	        Scale factor for KV cache.
496	    sm_count : Optional[int], default=None
497	        Number of streaming multiprocessors to use.
498	        If None, will be inferred from the device.
499	    enable_pdl : Optional[bool], default=None
500	        Whether to enable PDL (Persistent Data Loader) optimization.
501	        If None, will be set to True if hardware supports it.
502	
503	    Note
504	    ----
505	    The function automatically infers several parameters from tensor shapes:
506	    - batch_size from q.shape[0]
507	    - head_dim from q.shape[-1]
508	    - head_group_ratio is fixed to 128 for MLA
509	    - max_seq_len from page_table.shape[-1] * page_size
510	    """
511	    # Handle optional parameters
512	    if sm_count is None:
513	        sm_count = get_device_sm_count(q.device)
514	
515	    enable_pdl = enable_pdl if enable_pdl is not None else device_support_pdl(q.device)
516	
517	    # Infer parameters from tensors
518	    batch_size = q.shape[0]
519	    head_dim = q.shape[-1]
520	    num_q_heads = q.shape[-2]
521	
522	    # Calculate head_group_ratio (MLA has 1 KV head, so ratio = num_q_heads)
523	    head_group_ratio = num_q_heads
524	    if head_group_ratio != 128:
525	        raise ValueError(
526	            f"XQA MLA only supports 128 query heads (head_group_ratio=128), "
527	            f"got {num_q_heads} query heads"
528	        )
529	
530	    # Calculate max_seq_len from page_table and page_size
531	    num_pages_per_seq = page_table.shape[-1]
532	    max_seq_len = num_pages_per_seq * page_size
533	
534	    assert k_cache.dtype == v_cache.dtype, "K and V cache must have the same dtype"
535	
536	    if get_compute_capability(torch.device(device="cuda"))[0] not in [12]:
537	        raise RuntimeError("XQA MLA is only supported on SM120/SM121 GPUs")
538	
539	    xqa_module = get_xqa_module_mla(
540	        q.dtype,
541	        k_cache.dtype,
542	        page_size,
543	        head_dim,
544	        head_group_ratio,
545	        False,
546	    )
547	    xqa_module.xqa_mla(
548	        sm_count,
549	        q_scale,
550	        output,
551	        q,
552	        k_cache,
553	        v_cache,
554	        page_table,
555	        max_seq_len,
556	        seq_lens,
557	        batch_size,
558	        kv_scale,
559	        semaphores,
560	        workspace_buffer,
561	        enable_pdl,
562	    )
563

#include "../tvm_ffi_utils.h"
#include "mha.h"

using tvm::ffi::Optional;

#if MLA_WRAPPER
void xqa_wrapper_mla(int64_t multiProcessorCount, double qScale, Optional<TensorView> qScaleTensor,
                     TensorView output, TensorView q, TensorView kCacheVLLM, TensorView vCacheVLLM,
                     TensorView kvCachePageList, int64_t maxSeqLen, TensorView seqLen,
                     int64_t batchSize, double kvCacheScale, Optional<TensorView> kvScaleTensor,
                     TensorView semaphores, TensorView scratch, bool enable_pdl) {
  auto stream = get_stream(output.device());
  float const* qScalePtr = qScaleTensor.has_value()
                               ? reinterpret_cast<float const*>(qScaleTensor.value().data_ptr())
                               : nullptr;
  float const* kvScalePtr = kvScaleTensor.has_value()
                                ? reinterpret_cast<float const*>(kvScaleTensor.value().data_ptr())
                                : nullptr;
  // Extract strides from TensorView (in elements, not bytes)
  uint64_t kv_stride_page = kCacheVLLM.stride(0);
  uint64_t [REDACTED](-2);
  uint64_t kv_stride_head = kCacheVLLM.stride(-3);

  launchMLAFlashInfer(multiProcessorCount, 1, qScale, qScalePtr,
                      reinterpret_cast<OutputHead*>(output.data_ptr()),
                      reinterpret_cast<InputHead const*>(q.data_ptr()),
                      reinterpret_cast<GMemCacheHead*>(kCacheVLLM.data_ptr()),
                      reinterpret_cast<GMemCacheHead*>(vCacheVLLM.data_ptr()),
                      reinterpret_cast<KVCachePageIndex const*>(kvCachePageList.data_ptr()),
                      maxSeqLen, reinterpret_cast<uint32_t const*>(seqLen.data_ptr()), batchSize,
                      kvCacheScale, kvScalePtr, reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(semaphores.data_ptr()),
                      reinterpret_cast<void*>(scratch.data_ptr()), enable_pdl, kv_stride_page,
                      kv_stride_token, kv_stride_head, stream);
}
#else

void xqa_wrapper(bool run_sm90_fp8_mha, int64_t multiProcessorCount, int64_t nbKHeads,
                 int64_t slidingWinSize, double qScale, Optional<TensorView> qScaleTensor,
                 TensorView output, double rcpOutScale, TensorView q,
                 Optional<TensorView> attentionSinks, TensorView kCacheVLLM, TensorView vCacheVLLM,
                 Optional<TensorView> kSfCacheVLLM, Optional<TensorView> vSfCacheVLLM,
                 TensorView kvCachePageList, int64_t maxSeqLen, TensorView seqLen,
                 int64_t batchSize, double kvCacheScale, Optional<TensorView> kvScaleTensor,
                 int64_t qSeqLen, Optional<TensorView> mask, TensorView semaphores,
                 TensorView scratch, bool enable_pdl) {
  auto stream = get_stream(output.device());
  float const* attentionSinksPtr =
      attentionSinks.has_value() ? reinterpret_cast<float const*>(attentionSinks.value().data_ptr())
                                 : nullptr;
  float const* qScalePtr = qScaleTensor.has_value()
                               ? reinterpret_cast<float const*>(qScaleTensor.value().data_ptr())
                               : nullptr;
  float const* kvScalePtr = kvScaleTensor.has_value()
                                ? reinterpret_cast<float const*>(kvScaleTensor.value().data_ptr())
                                : nullptr;
#if USE_SM90_MHA
  auto const mha_func = run_sm90_fp8_mha ? &launchHopperF8MHAFlashInfer : &launchMHAFlashInfer;
#else
  auto const mha_func = &launchMHAFlashInfer;
#endif

  // Extract strides from TensorView (in elements, not bytes)
  uint64_t kv_stride_page = kCacheVLLM.stride(0);
  uint64_t [REDACTED](-3);
  uint64_t kv_stride_head = kCacheVLLM.stride(-2);

#if SPEC_DEC
  MaskType const* maskPtr =
      mask.has_value() ? reinterpret_cast<MaskType const*>(mask.value().data_ptr()) : nullptr;
#endif

  void* kSfCachePtr = kSfCacheVLLM.has_value() ? kSfCacheVLLM.value().data_ptr() : nullptr;
  void* vSfCachePtr = vSfCacheVLLM.has_value() ? vSfCacheVLLM.value().data_ptr() : nullptr;

  mha_func(multiProcessorCount, nbKHeads, slidingWinSize, qScale, qScalePtr,
           reinterpret_cast<OutputHead*>(output.data_ptr()),
#if LOW_PREC_OUTPUT
           rcpOutScale,
#endif
           reinterpret_cast<InputHead const*>(q.data_ptr()), attentionSinksPtr,
           reinterpret_cast<GMemCacheHead*>(kCacheVLLM.data_ptr()),
           reinterpret_cast<GMemCacheHead*>(vCacheVLLM.data_ptr()),
#if ENABLE_4BIT_KV_CACHE
           reinterpret_cast<GMemCacheHeadSf*>(kSfCachePtr),
           reinterpret_cast<GMemCacheHeadSf*>(vSfCachePtr),
#endif
           reinterpret_cast<KVCachePageIndex const*>(kvCachePageList.data_ptr()), maxSeqLen,
           reinterpret_cast<uint32_t const*>(seqLen.data_ptr()), batchSize, kvCacheScale,
           kvScalePtr,
#if SPEC_DEC
           qSeqLen, nullptr, maskPtr,
#endif
           reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(semaphores.data_ptr()),
           reinterpret_cast<void*>(scratch.data_ptr()), enable_pdl, kv_stride_page, kv_stride_token,
           kv_stride_head, stream);
}
#endif

> AGENT

这非常关键。`is_prefill = params.max_seqlen_q > 1`，对 sparse stage2，**max_seqlen_q == 1**（每个 token 一行），所以走的是 `decode_wrapper`，**不是 prefill_wrapper**。

Confirmed: 当 chunk 长度 >= dense_len (full sparse path)，**sparse_max_seq_len_q=1**, batch dimension 被展开到 `chunk_q_len * head_group_num` rows，每行只接 sparse-selected top-K block indices。这就是 nsys 看到的 `CTA_TILE_Q=16, NUM_MMA_Q=1` 形态（decode-style）。

现在确认 sparse stage2 kv_indices 性质：每 row 一个 sparse_topk * block_size 长度的 page index list。XQA 接 `page_table[batch_size, nb_pages_per_seq]`，**只要 batch_size = total rows, page_table 内容为 sparse-selected page ids, 形式上是兼容的**（每 row 把自己的 K 视为 contiguous "pages"）。但 page_size 还是阻塞。

`sparse_block_size=64`, page_size=1. 也就是 sparse stage2 KV 的 contiguous "block" 是 64 tokens, 但 FlashInfer 的 page_size=1 意味着这 64 个 token 的 KV cache 在物理上是被 64 个 page-1 slot 表示的（每个 page 一个 token），sparse 选 top-K 个 64-tokens-block 后，要把每 block 展开成 64 个连续 indices 写入 `kv_indices`。

title:	SM120 attention kernels exist but are blocked by wiring issues (fmha_v2, backend selector, MLA)
state:	OPEN
author:	blake-snc (Blake Ledden)
labels:	bug, op: attention, priority: must have (P0)
comments:	6
assignees:	saltyminty (Mingyang Wang)
projects:	
milestone:	
number:	2555
--
## Summary

We've done a deep investigation of FlashInfer's SM120 support on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121a, CUDA 13.0) and found that **SM120 attention kernels already exist in the codebase but are not wired into the runtime pipeline**. Three specific wiring issues prevent SM120 from using its optimized paths:

## Issue 1: FMHA_V2 SM120 kernels gated behind `ENABLE_SM120`

**Location:** `flashinfer/jit/attention/fmha_v2/generator_utils.py:6772-6786`

SM120-specific FMHA_V2 kernels are only generated if the `ENABLE_SM120` environment variable is set:

```python
if "ENABLE_SM120" in os.environ:
    enumerate_hmma_flash_kernels(specs, sm=120, dtype="fp16")
    enumerate_hmma_flash_kernels(specs, sm=120, dtype="bf16")
    # ...
```

Three SM120 kernel files are referenced in `jit/attention/modules.py:1918-1920` (BF16 and FP8 variants) but never get generated in standard builds. This means `gen_trtllm_fmha_v2_module()` can't find them at runtime.

**Expected:** SM120 kernels should be generated by default when building for SM120 targets.

## Issue 2: `determine_attention_backend()` routes SM120 to generic FA2

**Location:** `flashinfer/utils.py:455-497`

```python
def determine_attention_backend(device, ...):
    if is_sm90a_supported(device) and is_fa3_backend_supported(...):
        return "fa3"
    else:
        return "fa2"
```

This only checks for SM90. SM120 falls through to generic FA2 (Ampere-level), even though SM120-specific FMHA_V2 kernels exist. The function should have an SM120 path that routes to the fmha_v2 SM120 backend.

## Issue 3: `determine_mla_backend()` routes SM120 to FA2 instead of XQA

**Location:** `flashinfer/utils.py:561-562`

```python
def determine_mla_backend(device):
    return "fa3" if is_sm90a_supported(device) else "fa2"
```

SM120 gets `fa2` for MLA, but FlashInfer already has a functional XQA MLA backend specifically for SM120 (`data/csrc/xqa/mla_sm120.cu`, compiled with `supported_major_versions=[12]` in `jit/xqa.py:137`). This function should return `"xqa"` for SM120.

## What Currently Works on SM120

| Component | Status |
|---|---|
| XQA decode (MHA) | ✅ Works (`xqa.py` checks `[9, 10, 12]`) |
| XQA decode (MLA, FP8) | ✅ Code exists (`mla_sm120.cu`) but Issue #2166 reports failures |
| FMHA_V2 SM120 prefill | ❌ Kernels exist but never generated or routed to |
| SM120 GEMM (FP8, FP4) | ✅ Works via dedicated SM120 CUTLASS kernels |

## Proposed Fixes

1. Remove `ENABLE_SM120` gate in `generator_utils.py` (or enable by default for SM120 targets)
2. Add SM120 branch in `determine_attention_backend()` to route to fmha_v2 SM120 kernels
3. Add SM120 branch in `determine_mla_backend()` to route to XQA

## Environment

- NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM121a)
- CUDA 13.0, aarch64
- flashinfer-python 0.6.2+cu130
- PyTorch 2.9.1+cu130

Related issues: #1147, #2166, #2294

*From [Second Nature Computing](https://secondnature.pro) — testing on DGX Spark.*

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding FlashInfer XQA SM120/SM_120a Blackwell consumer prefill issues:

## Key Issues

On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), SGLang 0.5.10 routes MLA prefill/context through the TRTLLM MLA prefill path, which calls FlashInfer's TllmGenFmhaRunner and fails immediately with Unsupported architecture.

The trtllm-gen FMHA (Fused Multi-Head Attention) kernels used by flashinfer lack pre-compiled cubins for SM120 (RTX PRO 6000) and SM121 (DGX Spark GB10, RTX 5090). This blocks the trtllm-gen FMHA backend on all consumer Blackwell GPUs.

## user_4813494d Cause

SM120 (consumer Blackwell) does not have tcgen05 instructions or TMEM — it uses mma.sync.aligned.block_scale instead of tcgen05.mma. The SM100 FMHA kernel source cannot simply be recompiled for SM120; it requires architectural adaptation for SM120's instruction set.

## XQA Backend Status

However, SM120 gets fa2 for MLA, but FlashInfer already has a functional XQA MLA backend specifically for SM120 (data/csrc/xqa/mla_sm120.cu, compiled with supported_major_versions=[12] in jit/xqa.py:137).

## SM120 vs SM_120a Distinction

Only 120a or 121a targets unlock the dedicated NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA instructions. The prebuilt wheels for CUDA >= 12.9 compile all SM12x code with 120f, so neither SM120 nor SM121 gets native NVFP4/MXFP4 MMA in AOT-compiled modules.

The core issue is that consumer Blackwell SM120 GPUs lack TensorRT-LLM FMHA cubins, though FlashInfer does have SM120-specific XQA kernels available that need better wiring.

Now let me check the XQA grid dim, which tells us per-batch granularity. Already saw: `dim3 dimGrid{nbSubSeqPerSeq, nbKHeads (* nbTokenBlocksPerGrp), batchSize}`. This means **batch_size = number of sequences**, and `seqLen[i]` gives per-seq length. Pages are arranged as `[batchSize][maxNbPagesPerSeq]` contiguous list.

For our sparse stage2 with `max_seqlen_q=1` and `bs = chunk_q_len * head_group_num = 32768 * 16 = 524288` rows per layer per chunk (huge!), XQA would treat each row as one "sequence" with its own page table of `top-K * 64 / page_size` pages. Let me check the maxBatchSize:

state:	OPEN

## Motivation

- [ ] Recently, the community has been looking for improved SM120 support, so we'd like to improve the performance and usability across various models.

## Models
Some popular models requested:

- [ ] **DSA (not currently supported):**
    - [ ] `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2`
    - [ ] `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.2-NVFP4`
    - [ ] `zai-org/GLM-5-FP8`
- [ ] **MLA:**
    - [x] `nvidia/DeepSeek-V3.1-NVFP4`
    - [x] `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`
    - [ ] Use `fmha_v2_prefill_deepseek` for MLA prefill
    - [ ] Use XQA for MLA decode
- [ ] **GDN:**
    - [x] `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`
- [ ] **MHA:**
    - [x] `nvidia/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4`
    - [x] `baseten-admin/glm-4.7-fp4`

## Attention & Heuristics
- [ ] Enable XQA for MHA optimization #17115
- [x] Re-enable Flashinfer for full attention in hybrid models https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20604
- [ ] Add some better heuristics for attention backend selection (`fa2, xqa, cudnn`)
- [ ] Use CuDNN prefill and decode through Flashinfer API (`cudnn` decode also cannot be selected through the attention wrapper so it may need separate integration)
- [ ] Support Spec V2 (overlap scheduling + speculative decoding) in Flashinfer attention backend (currently, it has a sync from `plan_stream`). Currently, only `xqa` MHA can support this for SM120.

## Mixed Precision & Core Types (NVFP4 / MXFP8 / MXFP4)
- [ ] NVFP4 KV Cache #18314
- [x] MXFP8 functional enablement #19112 (Done)
- [x] MXFP4 functional enablement with `triton_kernels` #19718 #20040

## Backend & Kernel Optimization (CUTLASS/cuDNN)
- [ ] Support BF16 x BF16 GEMM from Cute-DSL example in CUTLASS repo, as currently, `torch.linear` will generate a kernel for Ampere architecture (SM80) (confirmed can be fixed by upgrading Torch)
- [ ] FP8 blockscale CUTLASS backend to replace Triton blockscale #18872 #20887
- [ ] Support MXFP8 grouped GEMM through CUTLASS
- [ ] Support MXFP8 dense GEMM through CUTLASS
- [ ] Support/Improve per-tensor/per-channel FP8 through CUTLASS
- [ ] Support MXFP4 x MXFP4 (investigate/benchmark if the current one is through cuDNN, or CUTLASS)
- [ ] Improve NVFP4 x NVFP4 (currently, cuDNN outperforms CUTLASS implementation in all scenarios, even though it has StreamK) #20047 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21314 
- [ ] Further improvement can utilize SwapAB in conjunction with mixed TMA recipe, perhaps both for dense and MoE GEMM.

### MoE specific
- [ ] Improve `--moe-runner-backend=flashinfer_cutlass` (`cutlass` is just a port of the `flashinfer_cutlass` version)
- [ ] Improve various small kernels overhead
- [ ] Support (if not already supported) fuse shared to routed experts
- [ ] Improve grouped GEMM (highest importance) on SM120
- [ ] Support BF16, FP8, and NVFP4, so ideally all of these can be improved
- [ ] Investigate why some users have reported `cutlass` is better than `flashinfer_cutlass`; aim to beat `triton` in all scenarios.

## Communication
- [ ] Support TRTLLM allreduce fusion and benchmark if it is faster
- [ ] SM120 for 6KD can support P2P communication through PCIe, but it doesn't support the feature of multicast. 
- [ ] Benchmark at various message and world sizes and see if there is any range which it is better.

## Architecture-Specific Support (DSA / MLA)
- [ ] Support DSA. Currently, it is a purely MLA based implementation, which is suboptimal. 
- [ ] Support paged MQA logits kernel
- [ ] Support other kernels through DSA that are from DeepGEMM.

### Flashinfer side
- [x] Enable SM120F compilation https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2650
- [x] Requires Flashinfer >= 0.6.4: Improve `mm_fp4` for SM120 https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2460
- [x] Group-wise FP8 for SM120 https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/1610 https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2721 #19721
- [ ] Blockwise FP8 GEMM/MoE for SM120 https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/issues/2728

### CUTLASS or TRTLLM side
- [ ] Study if we can integrate any CUTLASS or TRTLLM SM120 kernels not in Flashinfer.

We've completed hands-on validation and have corrections to the original report:

### Issue 3 Correction: `determine_mla_backend()` returning "fa2" is CORRECT

We validated that **FA2 MLA (`BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` with backend="fa2") works perfectly on SM120** with both BF16 and FP16:

```python
# Both pass on SM120:
wrapper = BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper(float_workspace_buffer=ws, backend="fa2")
wrapper.plan(qo_indptr, kv_indptr, kv_indices, kv_len_arr, num_heads=128,
             head_dim_ckv=512, head_dim_kpe=64, page_size=16, ...)
out = wrapper.run(q_nope, q_pe, ckv_cache, kpe_cache)
# → shape [4, 128, 512], no NaN ✅
```

So `determine_mla_backend()` returning "fa2" for SM120 is actually correct — the JIT-compiled FA2 MLA kernels work. The XQA MLA FP8 path (`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`) is a separate API that also works on SM120 but is FP8-only.

### Full Validated Results on SM120

| Operation | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| FA2 single prefill (BF16/FP16) | ✅ PASS | `single_prefill_with_kv_cache` |
| FA2 paged decode (FP16) | ✅ PASS | `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` |
| FA2 batch prefill paged (FP16) | ✅ PASS | `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper` |
| FA2 MLA decode (BF16/FP16) | ✅ PASS | `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper` |
| XQA decode auto/forced (FP16) | ✅ PASS | `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` correctly selects XQA |
| XQA MLA FP8 decode | ✅ PASS | `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` with float8_e4m3fn |
| trtllm-gen prefill | ❌ FAIL | "Unsupported architecture" at `fmhaRunner.cuh:30` |
| XQA MLA BF16 decode | ❌ FAIL | "XQA MLA only supports fp8 operation on SM120 GPUs" |

### Remaining Valid Issues

**Issue 1 (fmha_v2 ENABLE_SM120 gating)** remains valid — the SM120-optimized fmha_v2 kernels exist but are only generated with `ENABLE_SM120=1`. With `ENABLE_SM120=1`, `determine_attention_backend()` still returns "fa2" so the fmha_v2 kernels are never selected.

**Issue 2 (attention backend)** remains valid as a performance optimization — FA2 works but fmha_v2 SM120 kernels could potentially be faster.

**trtllm-gen prefill** failure is the biggest gap — `fmhaRunner.cuh:30` hard-fails on SM120. This blocks any trtllm-gen prefill usage on SM120.

Status update after reading the current code more carefully:

**Issue 1** (FMHA_V2 SM120 gated behind `ENABLE_SM120`): The `ENABLE_SM120` gate in `generator_utils.py:6874` only affects AOT builds (pip wheel generation). The JIT runtime path uses `generate_kernels.py`'s `enumerate_kernels()`, which generates SM120 kernels directly without the gate — and there's a dedicated `gen_trtllm_fmha_v2_sm120_module()` in `modules.py` that calls it. So this isn't blocking at JIT time.

**Issue 2** (`determine_attention_backend()` routes SM120 to FA2): Fixed by #2598 (open, pending review) — adds SM12x routing to a CuTe DSL backend, which works end-to-end on SM121a.

**Issue 3** (`determine_mla_backend()` routes SM120 to FA2): FA2 MLA works correctly on SM121a (validated). #2689 (open, pending review) adds BF16 XQA MLA kernel for SM120 as a follow-on improvement.

The main remaining gap is that if someone builds a pip wheel without `ENABLE_SM120=1`, the SM120 fmha_v2 kernels are excluded from the wheel. But that's only relevant for the fmha_v2/trtllm backend path — once #2598 merges, SM120 gets the CuTe DSL path instead.

Following up on your summary @saltyminty — you had it right on all three:

**Issue 1** (ENABLE_SM120 gate): Correct, not a JIT blocker. PR #2885 adds SM120 fmha_v2 to AOT pip wheel builds.

**Issue 2** (backend routing): Two PRs now address this from different angles:
- PR #2598 adds the CuTe DSL backend for SM12x (requires `nvidia-cutlass-dsl`)
- PR #3016 (just opened) enables the existing fmha_v2 HMMA kernels for SM12x standard shapes. The fmha_v2 JIT path already had SM120 kernel generation infrastructure but only enumerated DeepSeek MLA shapes — #3016 adds bf16/fp16 standard kernels and wires them into `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`. fmha_v2 is 10-31% faster than generic FA2 at S>=512 on SM121a.

When both are available, the priority would be: cute_dsl (if nvidia-cutlass-dsl installed) → fmha_v2 (for MHA S>=256) → FA2 (fallback). Each PR stands alone.

**Issue 3** (MLA backend): Correct, waiting on #2689 for XQA MLA BF16 bug fixes.
